Announcements
Win a HKD$100 Gift Card in Prize Draw! Recruiting CUHK Undergraduate Students (Aged 18–25) for a Study on Anxiety and Independent Life Skills!!  （可參加抽獎贏取港幣 $100 禮品卡！）誠邀中大本科生（18–25 歲）參與焦慮與獨立生活技能之關聯研究！ - Department of Educational Psychology
From: Esther Qiu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
estherxeqiu@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Recruitment Flyer
Project Title
A cross-cultural perspective on the association between anxiety and independent life skills
What is the study about?
In this study, we are interested in exploring whether and the extent to which independent life skills are associated with problematic behaviours (e.g., alcohol consumption) and mental health challenges (e.g., anxiety)
Who can take part?
You can take part if you are aged 18-25 and an undergraduate student at CUHK and can complete an online English survey independently.
What do we have to do?
You will complete an online English survey include questions about demographic information, educational performance, independent life skills, and mental health. The survey should take approximately 20 minutes.
What will participants receive?
As a token of appreciation for your time, participants will have the opportunity to enter a
PRIZE DRAW
to win a $100 HKD gift card.
One prize will be available for approximately every 10 participants
. If you wish to enter the draw, you will be asked to provide an email address at the end of the survey
Interested?
Please read more about the study and provide your consent here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_7P5Kp8XG88074vY
Note:Each participant can only participate once

From: Hannah NC Kong

hannahnckong@cuhk.edu.hk

Below is a student recruitment message for a research study from our research partner, HKUST Emotion and Personality Research Group.
---------------------------------------------------
Subject: Do research and get $300!
Dear students,
If you have 15 minutes now, please continue. If not, please come back later to enrol in this study.
We are inviting undergraduate students to take part in a study exploring the relationship between emotion and learning experience. If you are (1)
over 18 years old
, (2) are an
undergraduate student
, (3) have
lived in Hong Kong for at least 3 years
, and (4) can
read Traditional Chinese and speak Cantonese fluently,
please read on!
INCENTIVES
If you can complete Part 1, Part 3, Part 4 and at least 80% of the daily surveys in Part 2 for this study, you will receive HKD$300 supermarket e-coupon.
WHAT TO DO?
Part 1: Please complete a 15-minute survey now:
https://ust.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cJdIB3I81olJa5w
Upon completion of Part 1, you can download or update surveyYIK (iOS ver. 1.4.2 & Android ver. 1.4.1.97).
Part 2: Starting tomorrow (till 31 Dec), we will send you a notification each evening at 8pm during which you will complete a short survey
before midnight.
Part 3: In early Jan 2027, you will complete a 30-minute survey.
Part 4: In late Jan 2027, you will complete another 10-minute survey.
Please contact Jasmine via email at
happyu@ust.hk
or WhatsApp at 2358-5050 if you have any questions.
Best regards,
Jasmine Wong
HKUST Emotion and Personality Research Group

）

Healthy bones and muscles are the cornerstone of healthy ageing. Join us for “Say No to Falls & Fracatures” Public Health Seminar, organised in celebration of World Osteoporosis Day 2026, where leading healthcare professionals will share practical and evidence-based strategies on fall prevention, fracture prevention, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, nutrition, rehabilitation, and healthy ageing. The seminar will feature six expert-led talks covering a wide range of topics relevant to older adults, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.
Date: 11 October 2026 (Sunday)
Time: 10:00 am – 2:00 pm
Venue: Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA LT1), The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Capacity: 500 participants (Free Admission)
Registration & Enquiries: 2252 8796 (Office Hours) or QR Code online registration (registration link :
https://forms.gle/K8AuXWX6sHWj1vav9
)
Take the first step towards healthier ageing and learn how to say “No to Falls and Fractures”.

bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/25
»
Announcements
Are you a Self-Critical person? Cantonese Speakers Participant Recruitment[Free of Charge] Magic Chair Experiment 想跳出自責的循環？「魔法椅子」自我關懷對話實驗參與者招募【費用全免】 識廣東話【完成後可獲一份心理問卷報告】 - Department of Psychology
From: Chu Long Yiu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155211898@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「魔法椅子」自我關懷對話實驗 參與者招募 
心裡一直有把聲音告訴你不夠好？因此感到困擾，並想要減少批評自己？
香港中文大學心理學系 臨床心理科學實驗室 誠邀你參與有趣嘅心理學研究！
我們希望研究人們在受挫時，內心會如何與自己對話，而這些聲音會如何影響心理健康。
完成研究流程可獲一份心理問卷報告
招募對象：
年滿 18 歲
識廣東話
生活受自我批評困擾者
研究內容：
線上前測問卷
約 1.5 小時實驗室實驗
2 星期後線上後測問卷
地點：香港中文大學 王福元樓102室
有興趣參加？請透過以下連結報名：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_eJcE6LGxl0xhfW6
此研究已通過香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理的審核。
如有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡我們！
電郵： ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk（研究負責人 Yanbin）
—————————————————————————————————————————
Magic Chair Experiment – Recruitment of participants 
Is there an inner voice keep telling you that you are good enough? You feel distressed about this and wish to stop criticizing yourself?
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology at CUHK, is inviting you to join this interesting study.
We would like to know more about how people’s inner voice and interaction within oneself when facing struggles, and how these inner voice affects individual’s mental health.
You will receive a personalized questionnaire report after finishing the study.
 Eligible participants:
Aged 18 or above
Able to speak and understand Cantonese
Distressed about self-criticism
 Study Overview:
Online questionnaire before the experiment
In-person experiment at the laboratory (lasts for approximately 1.5 hour)
Follow-up online questionnaire at 2 weeks after the experiment
 Location: Room 102, Wong Foo Yuan Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T., Hong Kong SAR
 If you are interested in this study, please click the link below for application.
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_eJcE6LGxl0xhfW6
This study is approved by the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics (SBRE) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
 For enquiries, please feel free to contact Yanbin Xie at
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: Mindfulness Workshop: Connect Your Body, Mind & Nature－Certificate Upon Completion of All Four Sessions 【正念工作坊】連結身心與自然－完成四節可獲出席證書
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/25
»
Announcements
Mindfulness Workshop: Connect Your Body, Mind & Nature－Certificate Upon Completion of All Four Sessions 【正念工作坊】連結身心與自然－完成四節可獲出席證書 - Department of Educational Administration and Policy
From: Li Ching Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
心身連結正念工作坊
本工作坊旨在協助參加者學習正念的態度與技巧，連結當下的身心狀態，增進對韌性（resilience）及自然為本的療癒概念的理解，並透過五感體驗與大自然建立更深的連結。
日期及時間
正念基礎
：2026年11月3日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
覺察情緒
：2026年11月10日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
智慧的心
：2026年11月17日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
連結世界
：2026年11月24日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
地點
香港中文大學校園（崇基校園），活動將於戶外及室內場地進行。
語言
以廣東話為主，英語輔助。
重要事項
每位學生嚮導最少須參加兩節正念體驗工作坊。
首兩節工作坊為必須出席，參加者必須出席：
2026年11月3日：正念基礎
2026年11月10日：覺察情緒
能夠出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲優先考慮。
出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲發出席證書。
由於部分活動將於戶外進行，參加者請穿著舒適、適合戶外活動的衣物及鞋履。
本活動由香港中文大學教育學院
PDTL Grant
贊助。
計畫負責人及導師
劉雅詩博士
註冊中學教師
香港中文大學教育行政與政策學系高級講師
自2007年起致力向職前教師及在職教師推廣靜觀（正念）。
如有查詢，請聯絡李小姐：chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
成功報名的參加者將獲電郵通知。
Mindfulness & Body-Mind Connection Workshop
This workshop aims to help participants cultivate mindfulness attitudes and skills, develop a deeper connection with the present moment and their body-mind experience, and enhance their understanding of resilience and nature-based healing. Through experiential activities involving the five senses, participants will also have the opportunity to build a closer connection with nature.
Dates and Times
Mindfulness Foundations
: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
(Mandatory)
Cultivating Emotional Awareness
: 10 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
(Mandatory)
The Wisdom of the Heart
: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
Connecting with the World
: 24 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
Venue
The Chinese University of Hong Kong campus, Chung Chi Campus. The workshop will take place in a combination of outdoor and indoor settings.
Language
Primarily Cantonese, with English support.
Important Notes
Each student guide is required to attend at least two mindfulness experiential workshop sessions.
The first two sessions are mandatory. Participants must attend:
3 November 2026: Mindfulness Foundations
10 November 2026: Cultivating Emotional Awareness
Priority will be given to students who are able to attend all four sessions.
Students who attend all four workshop sessions will receive an attendance certificate.
As some activities will be conducted outdoors, participants are advised to wear comfortable clothing and suitable footwear for outdoor activities.
This activity is sponsored by the
PDTL Grant of the Faculty of Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
.
Course Trainer
Dr. Lau Ngar Sze
Registered Secondary School Teacher
Senior Lecturer, Department of Educational Administration and Policy,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Lau has been promoting mindfulness among pre-service and in-service teachers since 2007.
For enquiries, please contact Miss Fiona Li: chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
Successful applicants will be notified by email.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: Community Singing Performance: Join Us in Spreading Positivity! 誠邀參與「與風友同行」社區音樂計劃：用歌聲傳遞正能量與關懷！
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/25
»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
Community Singing Performance: Join Us in Spreading Positivity! 誠邀參與「與風友同行」社區音樂計劃：用歌聲傳遞正能量與關懷！ - The Nethersole School of Nursing
From: Chloe Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chloe.cheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀參與「與風友同行」社區音樂計劃：用歌聲傳遞正能量與關懷！
誠邀全校師生與中風人士及義工攜手參與「與風友同行」
社區音樂表演活動
。
參與意義
建立自信：協助中風人士重建自信心及自我價值感。
增強互動：提升中風人士與人溝通和互動的信心。
推動共融：鼓勵中風人士積極參與社區生活。

無需任何表演經驗
，歡迎所有熱愛音樂與社區服務的師生參加！
練習詳情
時間：隔週星期五 下午 2:00 至 3:30
地點：威爾斯親王醫院 香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 209室
註：未能出席恆常練習亦非常歡迎參加！團隊將提供歌曲及練習教材，參加者可自行練習，並於演出當日直接參與。
演出日程（可自由選擇合適場次）
10月7日 (三) 1:15 – 2:30 PM｜沙田 / 大埔區長者中心
10月31日 (六) 2:00 – 5:30 PM｜觀塘秀茂坪邨秀景樓外羽毛球場（照顧者嘉年華）
11月11日 (三) 1:15 – 2:30 PM｜沙田 / 大埔區長者中心
11月27日 (五) 1:30 – 4:30 PM｜九龍塘禮賢會彭學高紀念中學
12月8日 (二) 1:30 – 4:30 PM｜元朗聖公會白約翰會督中學
12月9日 (三) 1:15 – 2:30 PM｜沙田 / 大埔區長者中心
立即報名
網上報名：
https://forms.gle/ovyKk5WcSorrPrTT9
查詢電話：5726 1028 / 5463 8040
期待與您同行，用歌聲傳遞希望，讓更多人感受到社區的關愛與支持！
Community Singing Performance: Join Us in Spreading Positivity!
We warmly invite all students and staff to participate in the upcoming
community singing performance activities
. By performing alongside stroke survivors, students, and volunteers, we aim to help stroke survivors rebuild their self-esteem and confidence, boost their communication and social engagement, and encourage active community participation to showcase their resilience and potential.

No prior performance experience required
! All students and staff with a passion for music and community service are welcome to join.
Rehearsal Details
Time: Every second Friday, 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM
Venue: Room 209, The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, Prince of Wales Hospital
Note: Practice materials provided if you cannot attend regular rehearsals.
Performance Schedule (Choose the dates that fit your schedule)
7 Oct 2026 (Wed) | 1:15 – 2:30 PM | Elderly home in Sha Tin / Tai Po
31 Oct 2026 (Sat) | 2:00 – 5:30 PM | Sau Mau Ping Estate, Kwun Tong (Caregivers Carnival)
11 Nov 2026 (Wed) | 1:15 – 2:30 PM | Elderly home in Sha Tin / Tai Po
27 Nov 2026 (Fri) | 1:30 – 4:30 PM | Rhenish Church Pang Hok Ko Memorial College, Kowloon Tong
8 Dec 2026 (Tue) | 1:30 – 4:30 PM | SKH Bishop Baker Secondary School, Yuen Long
9 Dec 2026 (Wed) | 1:15 – 2:30 PM | Elderly home in Sha Tin / Tai Po
Register Now
Online Registration:
https://forms.gle/ovyKk5WcSorrPrTT9
Enquiries: 5726 1028 / 5463 8040
We look forward to having you join us in spreading hope through music and showing our community's care and support!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

From: Artist-in-Residence Programme
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
airp@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
2026
中大駐校藝術家徐秋雁演出
-
《豐饒之地，豐饒之身》
本年度駐校藝術家徐秋雁帶來《豐饒之地，豐饒之身》，一場融合歌唱、舞蹈與影像的跨媒體演出。作品以多種語言呈現，巧妙結合鋼琴與多種傳統樂器，並以祖先語言及原創音樂為創作靈感，圍繞母親、母性與大自然等主題，探索失落與悲傷，思考如何在困境中重新尋回希望與生命力。
演出結束後，曾參與徐秋雁工作坊的中大學生將與她攜手，呈獻一段特別的同台演出。
日期：2026年10月13日 (星期二)
接待︰晚上6:00 – 6:30
演出︰晚上6:30 – 8:00
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓低層地下利希慎音樂廳
入場：費用全免，不設劃位；名額有限，須預先登記。
對象：中大成員、校友及公眾人士

https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737058

Fertile Land, Fertile Body
by Jen Shyu
Experience
Fertile Land, Fertile Body
by Jen Shyu, a powerful performance combining song, dance and moving image across seven languages. Drawing on ancestral languages and original compositions, Shyu explores loss, grief and renewal through themes of motherhood, nature and ecological destruction.
After the performance, CUHK students who participated in Shyu’s workshops will join her on stage for a special collaborative performance.
Date: 13 October 2026 (Tuesday)
Time: Tea Reception 6:00pm – 6:30pm | Performance 6:30pm – 8:00pm
Venue: Lee Hysan Concert Hall, LG/F, Esther Lee Building (ELB), CUHK
Admission: Free Admission with limited seats. On First-come; first-served basis. Registration is required.

GenAI
親子工作坊」助教及培訓計劃（提供服務證書及酬金）
鑑於生成式AI（GenAI）在教育界的應用日益普及，學能提升研究中心（Centre for Learning Enhancement and Research）正與過百間中、小學合作，針對家長及學生舉辦一系列「GenAI親子工作坊」。工作坊由擁有19年教學經驗、曾獲行政長官卓越教學獎的資深教師設計及主講。
本中心期望招募對電子教學及人工智能輔助教學充滿熱誠的學生，成為工作坊的助教，幫助家長與學生正確掌握AI工具（如Gemini），提升學習效能並關注相關的資訊素養。
參與是次助教及培訓計劃的學生(2026/27學年)，將獲得以下寶貴機會：
專業認證：
支援最少3場工作坊或參與指定時數的相關教學設計)後，將獲本中心頒發服務證書。
實戰津貼：
在培訓及擔任工作坊助手期間，均可獲每小時港幣
84元
的酬金。
名師指導：
直接向獲獎名師學習教學實戰經驗，了解前線教學法。
前線體驗：
於中小學及中文大學校園內協助工作坊，親身接觸家長與學生，累積溝通與教學經驗。
參與計劃的學生須符合以下條件：
符合資格參加 香港中文大學「學生助理參與計劃」並已登記成為學生助理的全日制本科生（二年級或以上）或研究生均可報名參加；
操流利廣東話，能使用英語及普通話作簡單溝通；
掌握資訊科技教育及最新人工智能趨勢，樂於與學生及家長交流，熱衷於分享和展示人工智能的有效操作；
有補習、教學或編寫教學材料經驗者將有優勢；及
已完成認證為「
Gemini Certified Student (For University Students)
」。

bodyText:

[Invitation] Graduate School Seminar 2026: “AI in Education”  - The Graduate School Office
From: The Graduate School Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
gradschool@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[Invitation] Graduate School Seminar 202
6
: “
AI in Education
”
As
CUHK Graduate School
celebrates its
60th Anniversary
, we are not only reflecting on six decades of excellence, innovation, and impact, but also looking ahead to the future of education in an increasingly AI-driven world.
To mark this milestone, we are pleased to invite you to join us on 6 November 2026 (Fri) for a series of celebration activities
,
including our annual signature event, the
Graduate School Seminar 202
6:
“
AI in Education
”
, a
networking session
bringing together speakers, students, and alumni from diverse backgrounds and disciplines, as well as a
mini exhibition
showcasing the Graduate School’s history and achievements.
Jointly organised by the CUHK Graduate School and the Federation of Graduate School Alumni Associations (FGSAA), the
Graduate School Seminar 2026: "AI in Education"
presents a forward-looking dialogue on how artificial intelligence is transforming teaching and learning, research, and graduate education.
We are honoured to welcome three distinguished speakers who will share their insights on the evolving role of AI in education in keynote speeches and panel discussion:

"From Knowledge to Discovery: AI and the Future of Graduate Education"
Professor Irwin KING
- Pro-Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President (Education)
- Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Keynote Speaker & Panelist

"How Hong Kong Education City can Assist in the Implementation of the
Blueprint for Digital Education Development in Primary and Secondary Schools
"
Mr. Armstrong LEE
- Chairman, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK MBA
Keynote Speaker

"Standardised AI Literacy and Certification: Lessons from Southeast Asia"
Dr. Winson WONG
- Certified AI Trainer of United Nations University
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Keynote Speaker & Panelist
Dr. Tenny LAM
- Executive Director, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Panelist
Moderator:
Prof. Anthony SO, Dean of the Graduate School
Drawing on their diverse expertise across academia, education, and industry, our speakers will share insights on the opportunities and challenges presented by AI technologies, and discuss their implications for the future of higher education.
The Seminar will conclude with a
networking session with refreshments
, providing an opportunity for alumni, students, academics, and professionals to connect, exchange ideas, and explore new collaborations.

Date:
6 November 2026 (Friday)

Time:
3:00 pm – 5:30 pm

Venue:
VR Zone, Learning Garden, LG/F, University Library, CUHK
Shuttle bus service will be provided between University MTR Station and the CUHK University Library according to the designated schedule
Online Registration:
Please click
here
to register online via CUHK Registration and Attendance System on or before 23 October 2026 (Friday).
All CUHK, CUHK(SZ) and CUSCS students, alumni and staff are welcome to sign up for the event.
Join us as we celebrate 60 years of excellence and reimagine the future of graduate education at CUHK and beyond.

各位︰
為紀念國學大師饒宗頤教授（1917–2018）誕辰一百一十週年，香港中文大學中國文化研究所聯合香港大學饒宗頤學術館、香港浸會大學饒宗頤國學院、香港大學馮平山圖書館和學海書樓共同舉辦「饒宗頤教授紀念講座系列」。「頤學映真」專題講座由中國文化研究所主辦，特邀熟悉饒教授生平與學術成就的專家學者，從宗教史、考古學、書畫藝術等不同領域與視角，回顧、探討其學術貢獻與創見。第三場講座將於10月3日在香港中文大學舉行，誠摰邀請大家參與。

Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i: Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship
Professor Jao Tsung-i (1917–2018), renowned for his profound erudition in both the artistic and humanistic spheres East and West, had pioneered numerous research innovations. To commemorate the 110th anniversary of his birth, the “Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i” is co-organized by the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), Jao Tsung-I Petite Ecole at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology at Hong Kong Baptist University, Fung Ping Shan Library at HKU, and Hok Hoi Library. You are cordially invited to the lecture, themed “Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship” and hosted by the Institute of Chinese Studies, to be held at CUHK on 3 October.

Announcements
.【 $250 Coupon 】Recruiting Children (aged 11 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and Children's Emotional Health Development Study 誠意邀請11歲或以下兒童參加腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究-Department of Psychiatry.  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oscarwhwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

From: CHEUK KIT CHING
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【
《溝通障礙與科學專業文憑》（2027年1月入學）
開始招生
】
《溝通障礙與科學專業文憑》課程 (一年兼讀制) 現正開始招生﹐ 涵蓋言語治療之基礎理論及知識，並為學生提供臨床觀察機會，修畢此專業文憑者，更能在報讀香港中文大學於2028年度入學的《言語語言病理理學碩士》課程時獲優先考慮！
申請階段：2026年8月21日至11月30日
報讀表格：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13738399
課程資訊：
https://www.ent.cuhk.edu.hk/staud/prodipCODS/index.html
感謝各位踴躍參與已於
9月21日
舉行的首場課程資訊講座！
Facebook 專頁：
https://www.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=1586592669930765&id=100057401412127&rdid=XlDx6ySZdcLsvo8k#

尚未參加資訊講座的朋友，歡迎報名第二場資訊講座：

2026年10月24日（星期六）

下午2時至4時
簡介會登記表：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13739422
【
Enrollment Begins for Professional Diploma in Communication Disorders and Sciences
(January 2027 Intake)
】
The Professional Diploma in Communication Disorders and Sciences program (one-year part-time) is now open for enrollment, covering foundational theories and knowledge in speech therapy. It provides students with clinical observation opportunities. Completing this diploma will give priority consideration to those who apply for the Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology program at The Chinese University of Hong Kong starting in the 2028 academic year!
Application Period: August 21 to November 30, 2026
Application Form:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13738399
Course Information:
https://www.ent.cuhk.edu.hk/staud/prodipCODS/index.html
Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=1586592669930765&id=100057401412127&rdid=XlDx6ySZdcLsvo8k#
Thank you to everyone who joined our first information session on
21 September 2026
.
If you missed it, you are warmly invited to join our
second information session
:

24 October 2026 (Saturday)

2:00 PM – 4:00 PM
Info Session Registration Form:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13739422

多元文化親子體驗日
想同小朋友一齊認識唔同文化，享受一個充滿樂趣同學習嘅周末嗎？
誠邀您參加
多元文化親子體驗日
，透過多元化嘅互動活動，一齊探索南亞文化嘅獨特魅力！
  試穿南亞傳統服飾
體驗特色印度彩繪（Henna）
學習烏爾都語（Urdu）書寫
親子同樂，感受文化多元共融
呢個活動適合家長同小朋友一齊參與，透過輕鬆有趣嘅方式認識南亞文化，促進跨文化交流與理解。

特別獎賞：
首
8位成功報名參加者
可獲精美紀念品一份！

已報名及出席活動嘅12歲以下兒童
可獲發參與證書一張！

日期：
2026年10月18日（星期日）
⏰
時間：
上午11:30至下午1:00

地點：
Quarryside

名額：
20人
歡迎家長及小朋友參加
無需任何相關經驗
輕鬆有趣，適合一家大小

報名連結
：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3OsS8XjXGVdyCLc

查詢：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
快啲帶埋家人同朋友一齊嚟，透過體驗、交流同互動，感受南亞文化嘅色彩與魅力！
Family Cultural Experience Day
Looking for a fun family activity? Come and explore the rich and vibrant cultures of South Asia through hands-on experiences for both parents and children!
Try on traditional South Asian cultural attire
Experience beautiful henna drawing
Learn to write your name in Urdu
Enjoy a fun and interactive cultural experience together as a family
This is a great opportunity to learn about different cultures, celebrate diversity, and enjoy a meaningful weekend with your children.

Special offers:
The
first 8 registered participants
will receive a special souvenir!

Registered children under 12 years old
will receive a
Certificate of Attendance
.

Date:
18 October 2026 (Sunday)
⏰
Time:
11:30 AM - 1:00 PM

Venue:
Quarryside

Quota:
20 participants
Open to parents and children
No prior experience needed
Fun, family-friendly, and multicultural

Register here:

Join us to experience the beauty of South Asian cultures, make new friends, and celebrate cultural diversity together!

From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
大學通識教育基礎課程：2026-27學生活動資助計劃接受申請
各位同學：
自2012年始，大學通識教育基礎課程已在中大全面推行。UGFH和UGFN不知不覺已成為中大人的共同學習經驗。在2026-27學年，大學通識教育基礎課程將繼續推出
學生活動資助計劃
，鼓勵同學們自發設計、推廣及活化與課程相關的活動，在校園內外推廣經典閱讀，鼓勵校內外社群發掘閱讀經典的趣味及當代意義。
本資助計劃接受
個人或小組申請

Student Activity Fund (SAF)
to encourage student-initiated activities related to the two foundation courses. both individuals and groups
. We encourage diversified activities to promote classics reading, including exhibitions, reading groups, performance, APPs, websites and art designs, etc.  Each project should be completed within one year, and could be supported up to HKD 30,000.

bodyText:
Mass Mail System

»
2026/09/25
»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260928)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 28 September to 2 October: (1) Career Development & Further Studies (CDFS): All about further studies—where to study and how to sell yourselves to the university?, and (2) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
28 September (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30
29 September (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
30 September (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
2 October (Fri): 10:30 – 12:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 28 September to 2 October: (1) Grammar for the CRE. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心九月二十八日至十月二日舉辦 (1) 公務員綜合招聘試系列(CRE)：病句分析基礎, (2) 給故事一對 AI 的翅膀: AI編劇與影片創作工作坊, 及 (3) Happy Hour @ 占星之鏡：從個人星盤探索自我等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於九月二十一日至九月二十五日提供以下中文輔導時段。
28 September (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
29 September (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx
====================================
Contact us 聯絡我們
The Independent Learning Centre  自學中心
Address: Wu Chung Library, United College
Tel. No.：3943-8733 / 3943-8764
E-mail：ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

From: MSSc in Global Political Economy

Dear CUHK Students and Staff,
We are pleased to invite you to a special guest lecture by Prof. Hilary J. Allen, Professor of Law at the American University Washington College of Law, entitled
“AI, Fintech, and Techno-Solutionism.”

Date:
13 October 2026 (Tuesday)
⏰
Time:
4:30 pm – 6:00 pm

Venue:
LT2, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA), CUHK [
Map
]
About the Lecture
This talk will examine the growing belief that emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and financial technology, can provide solutions to complex social and economic challenges. Prof. Allen argues that this way of thinking, known as “techno-solutionism,” often oversimplifies structural problems by treating them as technical puzzles rather than addressing their underlying causes.
Prof. Allen will discuss how an excessive reliance on technological solutions can distract policymakers from pursuing meaningful structural reforms. She will also explore why it is crucial to critically assess the limitations and potential harms of proposed technological innovations, particularly in areas such as financial inclusion, market concentration, and privacy protection.
About the Speaker
Prof. Hilary J. Allen is a Professor of Law at the American University Washington College of Law. Her research focuses on financial regulation, fintech, and the societal implications of technological innovation. She is widely recognised for her critical analyses of financial technologies and their impact on markets, governance, and public policy.

We look forward to seeing you on 13 October.
Best regards,
MSSc in Global Political Economy

From: M.W.Leung

Dear all,
You are cordially invited to join a talk on 5 October (Monday), in which Prof. Don Kulick will discuss the labelling practices of people who define themselves as asexuals.
Title: The Lust to Name
Speaker: Don Kulick (Uppsala University & University of Hong Kong)
Date: 5 October, 2026
(Monday)
Time: 5:30-7:00pm
Mode: In-person
Venue: Room C2, 1/F, T.C. Cheng Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Look forward to seeing you at the Seminar!
Regards,
Department of Anthropology
Abstract:
This paper is a reflection on the labelling practices of people who define themselves as asexuals. People in this community vigorously and enthusiastically coin names for a wide variety of different (a)sexual orientations and proclivities – names from abroromantic to myrsexual to sex-neutral biromantic biaesthetic bisensual asexual, to many, many more. Prof. Don Kulick will discuss this enthusiasm in order to ask: What purpose does this lust to name serve? How did it originate and why is it flourishing now? What are some of the perhaps unintended consequences of such exuberant naming practices?

From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 15 October 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

醫護行社區藥房分享會：認識社區藥房服務

您有沒有想過，藥劑師除了配藥之外，還可以如何支援您和家人的健康？
誠邀您參加由
醫護行者（Health In Action, HIA）社區藥房
藥劑師主講的分享會，了解社區藥房如何透過不同服務協助您及家人管理健康，成為您值得信賴的社區健康夥伴。

日期：
2026年10月16日（星期五）

時間：
下午2時至3時

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海新里20號）

語言：
英語

講者：
醫護行社區藥房藥劑師

名額：
20人
您將會了解：
藥劑師在基層醫療中的角色
社區藥房提供的服務
藥物安全使用及藥物管理知識
輕微疾病及慢性疾病管理支援服務
藥劑師如何成為您可靠的社區健康夥伴
醫護行者相信，社區藥房可以成為大眾接觸醫療服務的重要第一站。透過健康教育、藥物管理及社區藥房服務，藥劑師能協助個人及家庭掌握健康資訊，促進身心健康。
本活動適合多元文化社群人士、社區工作者、照顧者，以及有興趣了解香港醫療服務的公眾人士參加。

https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K

成功報名並出席活動者，將獲贈精美紀念品乙份‼⭐
期待與您見面，一同了解社區藥房服務如何協助建立更健康的社區！
JCSATH

Sharing by HIA Community Pharmacy: Understanding Community Pharmacy Services

Have you ever wondered how pharmacists can support your health beyond dispensing medicines?
Join us for an informative sharing session by a pharmacist from
Health In Action (HIA) Community Pharmacy
and learn how community pharmacy services can support you and your family in maintaining good health.

Date:
16 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Venue:
Activity Room 1–3, Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay

Language:
English

Speaker:
Pharmacist from Health In Action Community Pharmacy

Quota:
20 participants
What will you learn?
The role of pharmacists in primary healthcare
Services provided by community pharmacies
Safe use of medications and medication management
Support available for minor ailments and chronic disease management
How pharmacists can become your trusted community health partners
Health In Action believes that community pharmacies can serve as an important first point of contact for healthcare services. Through health education, medication management, and community-based pharmacy services, pharmacists play an important role in helping individuals and families stay healthy and informed.
This session is suitable for members of multicultural communities, community workers, caregivers, and anyone interested in learning more about healthcare services in Hong Kong.

Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K
Places are limited and will be allocated on a
first-come, first-served basis
. Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation message.

Successfully registered participants who attend the event will receive a special souvenir!
‼⭐
We look forward to seeing you and exploring how pharmacists can support healthier communities together!
JCSATH

Trust Your Gut: From Early Life to Everyday Wellbeing TRUST YOUR GUT 齊來認識腸道健康   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

TRUST YOUR GUT 齊來認識腸道健康

您知道嗎？腸道的功能不僅僅是消化食物！腸道微生物群（Gut Microbiome）對我們的身體健康、心理健康、免疫力、睡眠質素以及整體生活質素都擔當著重要角色。研究顯示，我們的飲食習慣、睡眠質素、運動量，甚至壓力水平，都會影響腸道健康。
誠邀您參加這個內容豐富且實用的健康講座，一同了解如何透過簡單的生活習慣，促進腸道健康，提升整體身心健康。
認識什麼是腸道微生物群，以及它如何在生命早期建立
了解腸道健康、免疫系統及心理健康之間的關係
認識微生物群研究的方法，以及您如何參與相關研究
了解睡眠、運動、飲食及壓力如何影響腸道健康
獲取維持健康生活方式的實用貼士
無論您希望改善個人健康、關注家人的身心健康，還是單純對腸道健康感興趣，都歡迎參加！

日期：
2026年10月16日（星期五）
⏰
時間：
中午12:00 至 下午1:00

地點：
Quarryside

名額：
30人

語言：
英語（設有廣東話及南亞語言傳譯服務）

歡迎家長攜同子女一同參加。

報名連結：

查詢：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
一齊了解日常生活中的小習慣，如何為腸道健康帶來大改變，提升整體身心健康！
成功登記及出席將獲贈精美紀念品乙份‼⭐
Trust Your Gut: From Early Life to Everyday Wellbeing 
Did you know that your gut does much more than digest food? The gut microbiome plays an important role in our physical health, mental wellbeing, immunity, sleep, and overall quality of life. Research shows that what we eat, how we sleep, how active we are, and even our stress levels can influence our gut health.
Join us for an informative and practical health talk to learn how simple lifestyle choices can support a healthier gut and improve overall wellbeing.
Learn what the gut microbiome is and how it is established in early life
Know why it matters -- connections with gut health, immunity, and mental wellbeing
Learn how we study microbiome and how you can take part
Understand how sleep, exercise, diet and stress affect gut health
Get practical tips for maintaining a healthy lifestyle
Whether you are interested in improving your own health, supporting your family's wellbeing, or simply curious about gut health, this talk is for you!

16 October 2026 (Friday)

Venue:

Children are welcome to attend with their parents.

Enquiries:

bodyText:

CUHK Tang Chun-I Visiting Professor Fall 2026 - Public Lecture and Departmental Seminar  - Department of Philosophy
From: Ivy Ling
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
philosophy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Prof. Christopher Hitchcock will be joining the Department of Philosophy, CUHK as Tang Chun-I Visiting Professor Fall 2026 from 28 September to 23 October 2026.
Christopher Hitchcock, J. O. and Juliette Koepfli Professor of Philosophy, Caltech, is a philosopher of science whose research explores the variety of causal concepts that are deployed in the sciences, law, and everyday life. Hitchcock has worked on a number of other topics in philosophy including philosophy of biology, formal epistemology, experimental philosophy, and philosophy of language. His research is interdisciplinary, and he has published work in computer science, law, linguistics, and psychology.
Before joining Caltech, Hitchcock was on the faculty at Rice University from 1993 to 1998. He's had three articles selected by
The Philosopher's Annual
as among the year's 10 best in the field of philosophy (in 1995, 2001, and 2003). He has also received the Recent Ph.D. Essay Award from the Philosophy of Science Association, given for the best paper by a recent Ph.D. (in 1997–1998). He served on the governing board of the Philosophy of Science Association from 2002 to 2005 and was the president of the Society for Exact Philosophy from 2012 to 2014.
During the visit period, Prof. Hitchcock will deliver talks on a public lecture, a departmental seminar, and offer a 1-unit postgraduate course PHIL5180. Details of the public lecture and departmental seminar are as follows:
Public Lecture:  Causation Science and Everyday Life
Date: 28 September 2026 (Mon)
Time: 4:30pm-6:30pm
Venue: Cho Yiu Hall
Abstract:
Causation is a concept that plays a central role in the sciences, in law, in ethics, and in everyday life. Philosophers have been trying to offer analyses of the concept of causation for hundreds of years. In this talk, I want to highlight a particular challenge for this project. One the one hand, we investigate causal relationships using scientific methods—controlled experiments, mathematical modeling, statistical analysis, etc.—and incorporate them into our scientific image of the world. On the other hand, empirical evidence from psychology shows that when people make causal judgments, they are influenced by things like expectations, moral values, social rules, actors’ intentions, and other subjective and pragmatic factors. This raises the question of how one concept can answer to both descriptions: How can it be an objective part of the world described by science and also dependent on norms and expectations? I resolve this tension by showing how ordinary causal ascriptions serve a function such as an executive summary or an index (such as the consumer price index).
Departmental Seminar: Causal Models for Philosophy
Date: 12 October 2026 (Mon)
Time: 4:30pm-6:30pm
Venue: Room 220, Fung King Hey Building
Abstract:
Philosophers have adopted a variety of formal tools for use in philosophical projects. The early twentieth century saw philosophers turn to the new field of mathematical logic to address fundamental questions in philosophy; in the middle of the twentieth century many philosophers began to make use of probability theory; later in the twentieth century, decision theory found its way into philosophical theorizing. I will make a case for adding causal models, particularly structural equation models and graphical causal models, to the philosophers’ tool kit. It has been widely noted that causation is an ingredient in many concepts of interest to philosophers, which has often been used to motivate traditional “analyses” of causation. I will argue that causal models are often more useful tools than traditional analyses for shedding light on these philosophical concepts. I will support this claim with two illustrations: the Doctrine of Double Effect in ethics, and the propensity interpretation of probability.
Delivered in English | All are welcome | No online broadcast

https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13739649
Public Lecture – by 28 September 2026
Departmental Seminar – by 8 October 2026
For inquiries please email to
philosophy@cuhk.edu.hk
. Thank you.

From: Joanne HUI

嶺南文化研究計劃「嶺南文化研究論文獎」
2026-27
「嶺南文化研究論文獎」旨在推動國際嶺南文化學術研究，以鼓勵海內外在讀博士生及青年研究員在嶺南文化領域進行深入研究。
參獎資格：
本論文獎接受在讀博士生及青年研究員提交嶺南文化研究領域的優秀論文。論文內容可與古今文學、歷史、哲學、宗教、藝術、語言學、人類學等範疇相關。論文必須從未發表或出版，字數在三萬以內，中、英文皆可。
注意事項：
提交日期：2026年8月1日至2026年12月31日
參獎者須填妥申請表，並連同論文以電郵附件方式一併發送至：
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
，郵件標題為「嶺南文化研究論文獎2026-27（申請人全名）」。
報名表格
：
按此
查　　詢：
地　　址: 香港沙田香港中文大學中國文化研究所105室
電　　話: (852) 3943 7393
傳　　真: (852) 2603 5149
電　　郵:
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
Lingnan Culture Studies Research Paper Competition 2026-27
Organized by the Research Programme for Lingnan Culture, Institute of Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
The Competition aims to promote international academic research on Lingnan culture, as well as to encourage local and overseas doctoral students and young research fellows who are aspiring to conduct in-depth research in the field.
Eligibility:
1. Eligibility is limited to doctoral students and young research fellows.
2. Submissions must be papers of original research on Lingnan culture, in the areas of literature, history, philosophy, religion, arts, linguistics, anthropology, or other humanities disciplines.
3. Submission papers should be either in Chinese or English of no more than 30,000 words. The papers should never have been published.
Submissions:
Submission period: 1 August 2026 – 31 December 2026
Applicants should submit the application form along with the research paper by email to:
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
, with “Lingnan Culture Studies Research Paper Competition 2026-27 (Full name of applicant)” in the subject line.

Wish to transform your R&D results to a real business and become an entrepreneur?
If you wish to turn your research output into a real business, please consider applying for the
Technology Startup Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU)
. Or, if your students wish to commercialize their R&D results, please also encourage them to apply for TSSSU.
Successful applicants may receive
Up to HK$600,000 funding per year for potentially up to three years
Potential to join HKSTP’s Incubation Programme
Access to potential investors & industry partners
Mentorship from experienced entrepreneurship consultant
Apply Now IF
Your idea is innovative, your team is capable, your innovation and technology are unique and your business plan is sound
Your team wants to make a societal impact and is passionate about entrepreneurship
Eligibility of a PIC
The Person-in-Charge (PIC) of a CUHK TSSSU company must be a full-time CUHK student, a full-time CUHK professor, or alumni graduated within the last three years.
Compulsory Requirements:
The technology involved in the application must be CUHK-related
and with Intellectual Property (IP) owned by CUHK*.
The technology involved in the application must reach the required Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
Physical Science and Engineering technology must reach TRL 4 or above
and
HealthCare technology must reach TRL 3 or above
.

at least two
including the eligible PIC. Active members of CUHK should be the effective majority of shareholders of the Company.

7

agreement

* If a patent application has not been filed at the time of submission of a TSSSU-O or TSSSU+ application, the applicant should consider submitting an Invention Disclosure Form or a Copyright Disclosure Form and Assignment to the KTO IP and Technology Licensing Team.

香港中文大學教育學院「資優計劃」(PGT)定期舉辦春季、暑期及冬季資優課程，供小三至中六的資優學生參加。「資優計劃」現邀請主修相關學科的本科生或研究生擔任兼職助教，協助導師教學和支援學生學習。助教工作包括：跟進學生出席紀錄、分發課堂物資、支援學生學習、維持課堂秩序、留意學生學習進度、為缺席或有疑問的學生解釋課堂內容、策劃和組織活動、透過「資優計劃」社交平台協助內容創作與排版等。

2026
年
9
月
28
日
（星期一）
或之前前往
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/TA/recruitment
填寫網上報名表，並上載相關文件（個人履歷表、學歷證明文件副本（如香港中學文憑試證書）等）。
申請人必須出席面試，成功通過面試的助教須出席相關培訓，藉此認識「資優計劃」的教育理念、資優生特質、以及處理課堂突發事情的技巧等。面試及培訓均在香港中文大學校園內舉辦，並以粵語進行。有關詳情請參閲海報或瀏覽
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/_Doc/TA_Recruitment/Leaflet_JoinTA.pdf
。

Recruitment of Part-time Teaching Assistant (Student Helper) for the Program for the Gifted and Talented, CUHK
The Program for the Gifted and Talented (PGT) at the Faculty of Education, CUHK, regularly offers Spring, Summer, and Winter enrichment programs for gifted students ranging from Primary 3 to Secondary 6. PGT is now inviting undergraduate or postgraduate students majoring in relevant disciplines to serve as part-time Teaching Assistants, supporting instructors’ teaching and assisting students’ learning. Teaching Assistant duties include taking attendance, distributing learning materials in class, facilitating students’ learning, classroom management, monitoring students’ learning progress, explaining lesson content to students in need or those with questions, planning and organising program events, assisting with promotion via PGT’s social media platforms, etc.
Undergraduate and postgraduate students who are interested in becoming Teaching Assistants for the Program for the Gifted and Talented are invited to complete the online application form at
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/TA/recruitment
and submit the required documents (Resume, Certificates of public examination results, etc.) by
28 September 2026 (Mon
).
Applicants must attend an interview. Successful candidates will be required to participate in a training session designed to enhance their understanding of the Program, the characteristics of gifted students, and classroom management techniques. Both the interview and the training will be conducted in Cantonese and held on the CUHK campus. Please refer to the attached Poster or visit
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/_Doc/TA_Recruitment/Leaflet_JoinTA.pdf
for details.
If you have any enquiries, please contact us at 2603-7444 or 2603-7485.

中秋節將至，我們歡度佳節的同時，各種的送禮及慶祝活動往往會產生大量垃圾。為減少節日期間的垃圾，中大今年繼續參與綠領行動「月餅盒回收大行動」，收集到的月餅盒將送往環保署核准的回收商進行本地循環再造。
***中大收集日期：2026年9月28日（一 ）至10月9日（五）***

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students

2026/09/25
»
Announcements
Women's Voices, Shared Stories 一人一故事劇場 (Playback Theatre) 體驗  - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Women's Voices, Shared Stories

一人一故事劇場 (Playback Theatre) 體驗

「一人一故事劇場 (Playback Theatre)」(「一劇場」)是一種即興演出的劇場形式，結合了劇場、心理劇與原始民族聚會的儀式和精神。 在「一劇場」演出裡，主持人 會邀請玩場觀眾分享個人經歷，演出者隨即主動開放地聆聽、並以尊重的態度即興運用形體動作、音樂、戲劇的形式將故事演繹出來，作為禮物回饋觀眾的真誠分享。過程中，不同人士的真實生命經驗彷彿在互相對話，創造了一個空間，讓信任、人與人之間的共鳴共感，在整個群體中流動。
「一劇場」相信每個人都有故事可說，也有被聆聽的需要。
每個「一劇場」的演出都是一個連結過去、回應當下、擁抱未知的共同經歷；讓觀眾和演出者在分享與聆聽、展現與觀看的過程中，一同拆開生命和生活給所有人的寶貝、凝聚社群。
您是否曾希望有一個空間，能與其他女性交流、分享生活經驗，並感受到被聆聽和理解？
誠邀您參加這個溫暖而富創意的工作坊，讓來自不同文化背景的女性透過簡單的劇場活動互相認識、交流和學習。
無需任何戲劇或表演經驗
可自願選舉分享個人故事
可按照自己感到舒適的程度參與
在安全、支持和友善的環境中認識新朋友
透過劇場遊戲、故事分享、身體活動及小組反思，我們將一起探索女性在日常生活中的經歷、挑戰、力量與希望。

日期：
2026年10月11日（星期日）
⏰
時間：
下午3:00至6:00

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside  舍區 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海善里 20 號)

名額：
30位女性參加者

語言:
英語為主 (現場設有廣東話及南亞語言翻譯)
歡迎所有女性參加。無論您想分享、參與活動，還是單純聆聽，都非常歡迎您的加入。

歡迎攜同子女一同參與。

報名連結
：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0NfnDMKpKfjHgqy

查詢：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
期待與您一起分享故事、建立連結，並發現彼此的共同點

Women's Voices, Shared Stories
Playback theatre workshop
"Playback Theatre" — a form of improvisational theatre where actors listen, interpret, and use a range of expression methods and techniques to re-enact stories told live by the audience.
Have you ever wanted a space to connect with other women, share experiences, and feel heard?
Join us for a gentle and creative workshop for women from different cultural backgrounds to connect, share, and learn from one another through simple theatre activities.
No acting or theatre experience needed
Sharing personal stories is completely voluntary
Participate at your own comfort level
Meet new friends in a safe and supportive space
Through theatre games, storytelling, movement, and group reflection, we will explore women's everyday experiences, challenges, strengths, and hopes.
Date: 11 October 2026 (Sunday)
⏰ Time: 3:00 PM - 6:00 PM
Venue: Activity Room 1–3, Quarryrside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay
Quota: 30 female participants only
Language:  English (interpretation available in Cantonese and South Asian languages)
All women are welcome. Come as you are, whether you'd like to share, participate, or simply listen.
You are welcome to bring your children with you.
Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0NfnDMKpKfjHgqy
For enquiry, please contact JCSATH Whatsapp 61049535.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: West Lam

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[＊＊注意]
此次招募由
創新科技中心
發出，與中文大學知識轉移事務處 (KTO) 就同一個活動發出的招募為不同攤位，敬請留意。
各位學生：
由創新科技署舉辦的「創新科技嘉年華 2026」將於 24/10 至 01/11 於香港科學園開放給公眾人士參觀。為期 9日的展覽設有一系列與創科有關的互動及教育活動，包括本地發明及研究成果展覽、工作坊、互動遊戲，以及網上講座等。
創新科技中心 (CINTEC) 將聘用多名 student helper 協助 9日展覽的各攤位事務。
請留意 CINTEC 攤位與 CUHK 攤位為兩組獨立攤位，student helper recruitment 亦分別獨立進行。
日期：24/10 - 01/11（共九日；可以出席較多日期時段者優先）
時間：09:30 - 18:00（六、日）；09:30 - 17:00（一至五）
地點：香港科學園 第三期 12W 會議廳
酬金：$70/小時（包括 1 小時午饍時間）
工作：協助 9日展覽的各攤位事務
截止報名：05/10/2026 12:00 NN
報名表格：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742064
注意事項：
・僅供中大全日制學生應聘
・你必須為已完成登記學生助理參與計劃之同學，詳見 https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/programmes/student-helper-engagement-scheme
・非本地生必須提供入境事務處發出的「在校工作不反對通知書」，請參考 https://cpdc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/sites/cu_joblink/files/20241117%20-%20NOL%20(sample).pdf
・除非事前通知並獲本中心批准，否則不允許所有遲到早走之情況
・可以出席較多日期時段者優先
・中大創新科技中心（CINTEC）會在截止後透過電話或電郵聯絡合適的同學
・Student helper 會就當日情況，被分派至3個不同攤位
・當日早上會有 briefing 環節，以便同學了解各單位的工作內容
如有查詢，歡迎電郵 green-stem@cuhk.edu.hk 或致電 3943 8218。
香港中文大學創新科技中心
Dear Students,
"InnoCarnival 2026", organised by the Innovation and Technology Commission, will be held from 24/10 to 01/11 at the Hong Kong Science and Technology Park for the general public to attend. The 9-day exhibition consists of a series of innovation and technology related interactive and education events, including local innovation and research exhibitions, workshops, interactive games, and online webinars.
The Centre for Innovation and Technology (CINTEC) will hire multiple student helpers to aid with the 9-day exhibition at its booths.
Please note that the booths by CINTEC and CUHK are managed separately, and the recruitment of student helpers is also conducted independently.
Date: 24/10 - 01/11 (9 days in total; priority will be given to those who can attend more dates)
Time: 09:30 - 18:00 (Sat & Sun); 09:30 - 17:00 (Mon to Fri)
Venue: Function Hall, 12W, Phase III, Hong Kong Science Park
Salary: $70/hour (including 1-hour lunch break)
Duties: Assist with the operations of various booths during the 9-day exhibition
Application Deadline: 05/10/2026 12:00NN
Application Form:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742064
Important Remarks:
* Only full-time CUHK students are eligible to apply
* You must be a student who has completed the registration for the Student Helper Engagement Scheme. For details, please refer to https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/programmes/student-helper-engagement-scheme
* Non-local students must provide a "No Objection Letter for On-Campus Employment" issued by the Immigration Department. Please refer to https://cpdc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/sites/cu_joblink/files/20241117%20-%20NOL%20(sample).pdf
* Unless prior notice is given and approved by the Centre, late arrivals and early departures are not allowed
* Priority will be given to those who can attend more dates
* CINTEC will contact suitable students via phone or email after the application deadline
* Student helpers will be assigned to 3 different booths based on the situation on the day
* There will be a briefing session in the morning on the day to help students understand the work content of each unit
Should you have any inquiries, please feel free to email green-stem@cuhk.edu.hk or call 3943 8218.
Centre for Innovation and Technology (CINTEC), CUHK

各位學生：
由創新科技署舉辦的「創新科技嘉年華 2026」將於 24/10 至 01/11 於香港科學園開放給公眾人士參觀。為期 9日的展覽設有一系列與創科有關的互動及教育活動，包括本地發明及研究成果展覽、工作坊、互動遊戲，以及網上講座等。
創新科技中心 (CINTEC) 將聘用多名 student helper 協助 9日展覽的各攤位事務。
請留意 CINTEC 攤位與 CUHK 攤位為兩組獨立攤位，student helper recruitment 亦分別獨立進行。
日期：24/10 - 01/11（共九日；可以出席較多日期時段者優先）
時間：09:30 - 18:00（六、日）；09:30 - 17:00（一至五）
地點：香港科學園 第三期 12W 會議廳
酬金：$70/小時（包括 1 小時午饍時間）
工作：協助 9日展覽的各攤位事務
截止報名：05/10/2026 12:00 NN
報名表格：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742064

"InnoCarnival 2026", organised by the Innovation and Technology Commission, will be held from 24/10 to 01/11 at the Hong Kong Science and Technology Park for the general public to attend. The 9-day exhibition consists of a series of innovation and technology related interactive and education events, including local innovation and research exhibitions, workshops, interactive games, and online webinars.
The Centre for Innovation and Technology (CINTEC) will hire multiple student helpers to aid with the 9-day exhibition at its booths.
Please note that the booths by CINTEC and CUHK are managed separately, and the recruitment of student helpers is also conducted independently.

https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742064

* Unless prior notice is given and approved by the Centre, late arrivals and early departures are not allowed
* Priority will be given to those who can attend more dates
* CINTEC will contact suitable students via phone or email after the application deadline
* Student helpers will be assigned to 3 different booths based on the situation on the day
* There will be a briefing session in the morning on the day to help students understand the work content of each unit

You are warmly invited to join our upcoming
Translation Talk @ CUHK
, featuring
Dr. Daniel Canaris
from the
University of Sydney
.

Topic:
Will Over Intellect: Cross‑Cultural Translation and Moral Agency in Sambiassi and Xu Guangqi’s Discourse on the Soul

Date:
9 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
12:30 p.m.

Venue:
Room 214, Li Dak Sum Building, CUHK
This talk explores how Jesuit scholar Francesco Sambiassi and Confucian mandarin Xu Guangqi adapted Aristotelian psychology to Chinese thought, revealing a fascinating cross‑cultural dialogue between Western theology and Chinese moral philosophy. Dr. Canaris will discuss how their reinterpretation of the soul bridged scholastic metaphysics and Confucian ethics—an inspiring case of intellectual exchange across traditions.

Announcements
HK$250 Stipend: Two-Person fNIRS Experiments for Chinese Mainland Students-Come with your travel companion! 250港币酬劳: 双人近红外实验机会，面向中国大陆学生 – 与你的旅行朋友一起来体验吧！ - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Xiaohui RAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你对自己的大脑了解吗？你知道你跟小伙伴在交流对话过程中的共脑表现吗？不要错过这样一次难得的双人实验机会噢！！
本实验室使用临床级安全的近红外脑图系统，收集人大脑局部的耗氧变化，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：
Miss RAO,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
实验日期：5 Oct 2026 - 30 Oct 2026
实验时长：每次60-65分钟，共两次，可分别在同一天的上下午完成（包括实验准备20分钟，任务30-35分钟，填问卷5分钟）。
实验内容：1）佩戴近红外设备，参加互动实验，；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快/现金/百佳优惠券来支付250港元被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求：
1. 母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，听力正常；
3. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
4. 右利手（写字，用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
5. 实验当天不化妆，实验当天或前一晚在家自行洗头；
6. 可以接受在实验过程上戴上类似脑电设备的头套（实验结束后无需洗头）
7. 有共同旅游经历的两位同性别朋友，共同线下参与实验
8. 旅游经历发生在近两个月内，且旅行时间跨度2天1晚及以上
报名链接：
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
如有问题，请联系饶女士（1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk）
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
English Version:
Do you know your own brain? Are you curious about the inter-brain synchrony between you and your partner during communication and conversation? Don't miss out on this rare opportunity to participate in a two-person experiment!
Our laboratory utilizes a clinical-grade, safe functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) system to collect localized oxygenation changes in the human brain. This process is completely safe and does not cause any harm to the human body.
Experiment Date
: 5 Oct 2026 - 30 Oct 2026
Duration:
60-65 minutes per session, two sessions in total. Sessions can be completed consecutively in the morning and afternoon of the same day (including 20 mins preparation, 30-35 mins tasks, and 5 mins questionnaire).
Content:
1) Wear an fNIRS device and participate in an interactive experiment; 2) Complete questionnaires.
Location:
Room G34, G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building (Department of Linguistics), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK).
Compensation:
Upon completion, a stipend of HK$250 will be paid via FPS, cash, or ParknShop vouchers.
Participants need to meet the following requirements:
1. Native Mandarin speaker;
2. Normal vision (after correction) and normal hearing;
3. No brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological diseases; no scalp trauma or infection;
4. Right-handed (e.g., writing, using chopsticks);
5. No make-up on the day of the experiment; wash hair at home on the day of or the night before the experiment;
6. Comfortable wearing an EEG-like cap during the experiment (no need to wash hair afterwards);
7. Two same-gender friends/colleagues with a shared travel experience, participating in the experiment together in person;
8. The travel experience occurred within the last two months, and the trip lasted for at least 2 days and 1 night.
Enrolment link:
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact Miss Rao (1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk)
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

For request submissions, please submit them at

For enquiries, please write to:

「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，兩場知識與美學兼具的專題講座將於10 月 25 日（日）及11 月 28 日（六）在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行。
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries, features two insightful talks exploring the aesthetic side of Lingnan.  Two lectures will be held at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 25 October (Sunday) and 28 November (Saturday).
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

From: Winifred Wong

香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What will you do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).

香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What will you do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Subject: 研究資助局公眾講座 - 數碼社會：文化保育與網上訂價(Research Grants Council Public Lectures to be conducted in Cantonese)
香港高等院校進行了很多令人振奮的學術研究計劃。為了讓市民更了解本地研究的重要性及價值，研究資助局定期舉辦公眾講座，向大眾分享最新研究成果。
研資局將於今年﹙2026﹚舉辦一系列與STEAM教育相關的公眾講座，講題包括人工智能與文物保育、網上訂價、兒童教育及宇宙探索。這些講座旨在提升市民對相關方面最新研究成果的認識。講座詳細內容如下：講座以粵語進行。免費入場，座位先到先得，有興趣人士亦可於網上收看講座現場直播或稍後重温。詳細內容如下：(
https://www.ugc.edu.hk/big5/rgc/about/events/lectures/lectures.html
)
The Hong Kong higher education sector has undertaken many exciting academic research projects. To raise public awareness of the significance and values of the local research work, the Research Grants Council regularly organises public lectures to share the latest research results with the public.
This year (2026), the RGC has organised a series of public lectures related to STEAM education, covering topics including cultural preservation with artificial intelligence, online pricing, children education, and universe exploration (conducted in Cantonese). These lectures aim to enhance the awareness of the latest researches in related areas. Please refer to Chinese version for more details.

體育運動科學系，香港中文大學

發件人：何文柯
如有任何問題，請聯繫：
wenke.he@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學體育運動科學系運動營養與體力活動實驗室
誠邀您參加一項運動幹預研究!本研究將有助於瞭解您的運動代謝表現並提高您的代謝健康。
研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。
平時運動較少（每星期少於 150 分鐘中等強度體能活動、少於 75 分鐘劇烈強度體能活動，或二者同等組合）。
過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。
⏳
您需要做什麼？（
3
次評估
+ 12
周幹預訓練）
本研究為期 12 週，合格者將隨機分配至對照組、有氧運動組A、有氧運動組B，期間需前往香港中文大學實驗室進行 3 次評估，具體包括：問卷調查、空腹靜脈抽血檢測、指尖採血、身體成分測量、運動代謝測試。為減少測試過程中的不適感，運動代謝測試將與其他健康測試分開進行，整個研究過程中，您總共需要到達實驗室
6
次。

3
