You will receive
HK$50 CASH
for each valid submission.
Cash payment — not a coupon or voucher
Multiple submissions from different locations are welcome
No cap on the total participation payment
How to Participate?
If you are interested in participating in this study, please contact us through any of the following methods:
WhatsApp: 69736364 / 95124618
WeChat: gyq125229
Email:
yuGong@link.cuhk.edu.hk
/
1155213466@link.cuhk.edu.hk
After receiving your message, we will provide detailed photo-taking instructions and information on how to submit your photos.
Privacy and Data Protection
All information you provide will be handled confidentially and used solely for this research study.
Please feel free to share this information with anyone who may be interested.
Thank you for your interest and support! Your photos will help us better understand Hong Kong’s urban visual environment.

From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 15 October 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

15 October 2026 (Thursday)
Time:

Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

骨骼與肌肉健康是健康老齡化的重要基石。誠邀您參加香港骨質疏鬆基金會「肌骨守護．安行無憂」健康講座，與多位專家一同探討防跌、防骨折、骨質疏鬆症、肌少症、營養及健康樂齡規劃等重要課題。

Healthy bones and muscles are the cornerstone of healthy ageing. Join us for “Say No to Falls & Fracatures” Public Health Seminar, organised in celebration of World Osteoporosis Day 2026, where leading healthcare professionals will share practical and evidence-based strategies on fall prevention, fracture prevention, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, nutrition, rehabilitation, and healthy ageing. The seminar will feature six expert-led talks covering a wide range of topics relevant to older adults, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.
Date: 11 October 2026 (Sunday)
Time: 10:00 am – 2:00 pm
Venue: Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA LT1), The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Capacity: 500 participants (Free Admission)

Recruitment of Student Ambassadors Participate in “Intergenerational Inclusion” Health Activities Learn to Communicate with Older Adults & Understand Their Health Needs (Subsides available for ≥70% attendance) 招募學生大使參與「長幼共融」健康活動 學習與長者溝通及了解健康需要（出席率達七成可獲車馬費津貼） - The CUHK Jockey Club Institute of Ageing
From: Institute of Ageing
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kencheungiage@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The CUHK Jockey Club Institute of Ageing’s Elder Academy will launch “Healthy Ageing Programme” from October to November 2026. The programme consists of ten sessions, including exercise training, nutrition & cooking activities, and a community field trip.
We are now recruiting
five CUHK students
to join the programme as
Student Ambassadors
. Participants will accompany older adult learners during the activities, gain hands-on experience interacting with them, learn about their health needs, and assist instructors throughout the sessions to promote intergenerational harmony.
Programme Details
1. Intergenerational Exercise Training (7 sessions)
Learn about the importance of physical activity for older adults’ physical and mental well-being, and assist in exercises focusing on muscle strengthening, balance enhancement, and fall prevention.
Dates: 6 October – 24 November 2026 (Every Tuesday, except 17 November)
Time: 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Instructor: Certified Fitness Trainer
Venue: Yoga Eden, Chung Chi College, CUHK
2. Nutrition Workshop & Cooking Class (2 sessions)
Understand nutritious diet and participate in cooking healthy recipes.
Date: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday)
Time:
Workshop: 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Cooking Class: 1:00 PM – 4:00 PM
Instructor: Nutritionist
Venue: CUHK Classroom & Activity Room
3. Community Field Trip (1 session)
A guided visit to explore community fitness facilities designed for older adults.
Date: 26 November 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM
Instructor: Certified Fitness Trainer
Location: Tseung Kwan O District
Eligibility
CUHK students
Fluent in Cantonese
Enjoy communicating with older adults
Willing to assist and participate in programme activities
Subsidy:
≥70% attendance (at least 7 sessions): HK$700
≥ 90% attendance (at least 9 sessions): HK$900
Selected applicants will be notified by phone. Participation will be confirmed after phone verification by programme staff.
Application
If interested, please complete the online application form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_42h5AzwMhno6Rh4
Deadline: 27 September 2026 (Sunday), 11:59 PM

We are now recruiting
five CUHK students
to join the programme as
Student Ambassadors
. Participants will accompany older adult learners during the activities, gain hands-on experience interacting with them, learn about their health needs, and assist instructors throughout the sessions to promote intergenerational harmony.

Instructor: Certified Fitness Trainer
Venue: Yoga Eden, Chung Chi College, CUHK

Instructor: Nutritionist
Venue: CUHK Classroom & Activity Room

Time: 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM
Instructor: Certified Fitness Trainer
Location: Tseung Kwan O District

CUHK students

ericacheng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are recruiting volunteer native speakers of Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, and/or Tagalog to assist with recording a list of vocabulary items and short phrases. This project aims to support children from ethnically diverse backgrounds in learning Cantonese, English, and their home languages.
You must be:
1. Aged 18 or above;
2. A native speaker of Hindi, Punjabi, Tagalog, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
3. Able to read Hindi, Punjabi, Tagalog, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
4. Able to perform the recording task on the CUHK campus.
Non-CUHK volunteers are also welcome.
Details:
•
Location:
Academic Building No. 2, CUHK
•
Duration:
Approximately 1.5–2 hours
•
Task:
You will be asked to audio record a set of vocabulary items and short phrases in the language(s) you speak.
If you are interested, please fill in the form via the following link: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741813

==========================================
MCNS課程致力培訓治療師、護士及其他醫護專業人員，教授中風及其他腦神經疾病的最新專業知識與臨床技能 課程設有多元化實踐教學，同學可將課堂所學應用於專業實踐，進一步提升臨床及專業能力，為日後的專業發展及職涯晉升奠定基礎。
The MCNS program is dedicated to equipping therapists, nurses, and other healthcare professionals with the latest knowledge and clinical skills in stroke and neurological care.With hands-on practicum sessions built right into the curriculum, students bridge the gap between theory and real-world practice, sharpening their expertise and building a strong foundation for future career advancement.

From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Students,
Has writing always felt more like an art than an assignment to you? Ever wanted to share big ideas and worthwhile reads? Eager to connect with like-minded students who love writing as much as you? Here comes the perfect chance!
CUriosity
is CUHK’s campus magazine – made by students, for students. For 10 years, we published our thoughts and stories to students in CUHK through magazine publications, which are kindly supported by the General Education Foundation Programme of the Office of University General Education. Our latest issue, Issue 9, will come out soon! (For all of our issues, please go to our instagram @curiositycuhk).
We are now  recruiting
Leadership Positions, Core Members, Writers and Illustrators
for
CUriosity
’s Issue 10! We’re looking for someone dedicated and passionate about collaboration and writing!
Below are the positions for which we are recruiting:
Co-editor-in-chief
Marketing manager
Administrative coordinator
Core members
Writers
Illustrators
Designers
For a description of the above positions, you can check the document here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PQeZ-7eG-E5FfsLpHcDS9Ty5p9HYbakAhhM06fq1eR8/edit?usp=sharing
Whether you are an experienced writer or an emerging voice, we would love to have you! If you are interested, please submit your application here:
https://forms.gle/zVcGK7PDAPU4kmHE7
. For any enquiries, please write to us at
curiositycuhk@gmail.com
.
We look forward to having you on the team!
The

Team

bodyText:

Free Prostate Health Screening‼‼ 免費前列腺健康篩查－誠邀合資格男士參加 - S.H. Ho Urology Centre, Department of Surgery
From: Yellow Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
根據衛生署數據，前列腺癌是本港男性常見的癌症之一。透過及早篩查，可以有效降低相關的健康風險。本次活動由中大何善衡泌尿中心舉辦，為合資格人士提供免費的前列腺特異抗原 (PSA) 檢測服務。
活動地點： 沙田區（詳細地址將於成功報名後通知）
活動內容：(所需時間約一小時)
1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。
2. 前列腺篩查：合資格人士可獲免費前列腺特異抗原（PSA）測試乙次.
• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。
參加資格：
• 性別：男性
• 年齡：50-75歲
• 從未接受前列腺相關檢查
如有興趣參加活動，請填妥以下表格。
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
如想了解更多關於前列腺癌風險的評估, 可瀏覽以下網址;
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cance
r
參加者提供的所有資料將會被保密。如有任何查詢，請與我們聯絡 （Whatsapp: 5160 6904；電郵：yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk）。
According to data from the Department of Health, prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers among men in Hong Kong. Early screening can effectively reduce related health risks. This event is organized by the S.H. Ho Urology Centre of CUHK, providing free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) testing services for eligible individuals.
Event Venue: Shatin District (the exact address will be provided after successful registration)
Event Details: (Estimated duration: about one hour)
Video Presentation: An easy-to-understand introduction to the examination and treatment of prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate Screening: Eligible participants will receive one free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test.
Testing Method: We will collect blood samples from participants via a fingertip blood test and conduct an on-site PSA test using a PSA testing device. Results will be available in about ten minutes.
Eligibility:
Gender: Male
Age: 50-75 years old
Have never undergone any prostate-related examination
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the online form below;
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
For more information about the assessment of prostate cancer risk, please visit the following website:
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cancer
All information provided by participants will be kept confidential. For any enquiries, please contact us (WhatsApp: 5160 6904; Email: yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk)

【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀3歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 33個月或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿3歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on the gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between the gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is under 33 months old (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 3 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

Large amounts of data are now being produced, collected, and analysed at unprecedented speed, breadth, depth, and scale. Focusing on the development and application of computational methods for complex and large-scale human behavior and behavioral change, Computational Social Science addresses fundamental questions about individuals and collectives, and major social problems. With the aim to promote interdisciplinary collaborations in addressing substantive social science questions, the
CSSL@CUHK
was formed in April 2021.

GO!
共塑可持續校園

綠色辦公室計劃（綠識辦，又稱「GO!」） 自2012年推出以來，一直鼓勵中大同事齊心同行，將可持續發展理念融入日常辦公室運作
令人振奮的是，中大於2023至2025年連續三年，均有逾90個辦公室榮獲「實力綠識辦」殊榮 計劃更設立了優異獎、金獎、鉑金獎等多個類別獎項，以表揚及嘉許各部門在推動可持續發展與綠色職場文化上的傑出表現
中大社群透過一系列實際行動，展現對可持續發展的承擔，實踐聯合國可持續發展目標（SDGs）12「負責任消費與生產」及  目標13「氣候行動」 攜手為可持續的未來出一分力
了解更多「綠識辦」嘉許制度：
https://srsdo.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-hk/go/recognition/
GO! C
o-create a Sustainable
Campus

The Green Office Programme (GO!) has been encouraging CUHK colleagues to work together since its launch in 2012, integrating sustainability into daily office operations and promoting a culture of sustainability across campus.
We are thrilled to share that for three consecutive years (2023–2025), over 90 offices have been recognized as 'Competent Green Offices' The programme also features Merit, Gold, Platinum, and various category awards to commend departments for their outstanding performance in driving sustainability and a green workplace culture
Through a wide range of practical actions, the CUHK community demonstrates its commitment to sustainability by advancing SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production and SDG 13: Climate Action Through collective efforts, we are contributing to a more sustainable future
Learn more about the Green Office Recognition:
https://srsdo.cuhk.edu.hk/en-gb/go/recognition/

The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 21 September to 25 September: (1) Building a Bigger and Better Vocabulary, (2) Preparing for the Common Recruitment Examination (CRE) - Use of English (UE), (3) Hong Kong Civil Service Interview Preparation, and (4) Global Citizenship Series: Intercultural Communication. From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)

Ladies Only: Yoga & Tea Tasting Workshop

Looking for some time to relax, recharge, and focus on your wellbeing?
Join us for a special Yoga & Tea Tasting Workshop as part of
JCSATH Multicultural Awareness Week 2026
. This beginner-friendly session combines gentle restorative yoga with a mindful tea tasting experience to support both physical and mental wellbeing.
Date: 12 October 2026 (Monday)
Time: 10:00 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.
Venue: Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay
Instructor: Female Instructor from Curiouslyoga
Language: English
Quota: 15 female participants only
No previous yoga experience is required. Beginners are warmly welcome!
The workshop includes:
Gentle restorative yoga practice
Relaxation and mindfulness exercises
Guided tea tasting experience
A chance to connect with women from different cultural backgrounds
What to wear:
Participants are encouraged to wear comfortable clothing suitable for light stretching and movement (e.g. T-shirt, sportswear, leggings, loose trousers). Please avoid restrictive clothing. No special yoga equipment is required.
Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_d4EdKaH4WmLV1YO
Places are limited to 15 participants and registration is on a first-come, first-served basis. Successful applicants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation message.
We look forward to spending a peaceful and refreshing morning with you!

Announcements
【Overweight and Central obesity research, diet + exercise】 Recruiting individuals with central obesity aged 40-64 in the study  【中央肥胖研究，飲食+運動】中央肥胖改善計劃誠邀40-64歲合資格人士參與 - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education; Program Director: Prof. Eric Tsz-chun POON
From: HE Ye
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
heye@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學體育運動科學系誠邀中央肥胖人士參與健康管理研究！
研究目的：
中央肥胖與血糖異常、心血管疾病及其他代謝健康問題的風險增加有關。為應對這一公共健康挑戰，香港中文大學體育運動科學系正開展健康生活方式計劃，提供個人化健康支援。
參加條件：
年齡：40-64歲
平時少做運動/無規律運動習慣
中央肥胖：男性腰圍 ≥ 90 cm; 女性腰圍 ≥ 80 cm
過去三個月體重變動≤5%
現時沒有服用長期藥物
參加方法：
掃描海報二維碼或通過鏈接作網上登記【https://forms.gle/aBCMAHiFKdDK6z5L6】
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的健康生活方式計劃
參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02室
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
何小姐
WhatsApp: 94463265
電郵: sspe.project0716@gmail.com
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有檢測結果加密儲存，僅供研究團隊匿名分析，您可隨時要求刪除個人資料
[
歡迎邀請身邊感興趣的親友參加
]
Study Purpose:
Central obesity is associated with an increased risk of abnormal glucose regulation, cardiovascular disease, and other metabolic health problems. To help address this growing public health concern, the Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is launching a Healthy Lifestyle Program that offers personalized health support for individuals with central obesity.
Recruitment criteria:
Aged between 40 and 64 years
No regular exercise habits
Central obesity: waist circumference ≥ 90 cm for men and ≥ 80 cm for women
Body weight fluctuation ≤5% in the past three months
Not taking any chronic medication
Study arrangement:
Scan the QR code to register (https://forms.gle/aBCMAHiFKdDK6z5L6)
The study team will select participants based on the registration information
Arrange screening time
Arrive at CUHK Kwok Sports Building for the test
If you are eligible, you will be randomly assigned to start the formal Healthy Lifestyle Intervention Program
Study Location:
Room G02, Kwok Sports Building, Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin
Contact Us
If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Ms. He
WhatsApp: 94463265
Email: sspe.project0716@gmail.com
[Data safety] All data obtained during the study will be kept strictly confidential
.
[Welcome to invite friends and family who are interested to participate in our study]

NEWLY LAUNCHED! - UGEB2996 Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist (Fully Online & Asynchronous Learning) 全新推出！UGEB2996 初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色 (全網上非同步學習) - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。
課程特色
自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

Course Code:
UGEB2996

Course Title:
Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

Mode:
Online Asynchronous

Credits:
1 Unit

🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。

自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

日期：2026年10月15日（星期四）
時間：下午3時至4時30分
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地庫進學園虛擬實境空間
主持：香港中文大學中國語言及文學系高級講師張詠梅博士
語言：粵語
講座簡介：本講座將從葉先生筆下有關花鳥蟲魚及其他題材的散文出發，延伸至其他作品、尤其是他日記中的觀察記述、探討其如何在日常經驗中體察生活與藝術、並展現深厚的人文修養。
講者簡介：許鞍華導演，香港新浪潮電影代表人物，曾任香港電影導演會會長、香港國際電影節協會副主席。自1979年首次執導劇情片《瘋劫》，至今導演逾三十部電影，獲奬無數，包括曾六次獲香港電影金像奬最佳導演，三次獲台灣電影金馬奬最佳導演，2011年獲亞洲電影大奬頒發終身成就奬，2020年獲第77屆威尼斯電影節授予「終身成就金獅獎」，成為全球首位獲得該獎項的女導演。曾多次將文學作品搬上大銀幕，包括改編自張愛玲小說《傾城之戀》（1984）、《半生緣》（1997）、《第一爐香》（2021），改編自金庸武俠小說《書劍恩仇錄》（1987）和下集《香香公主》（1987），以及蕭紅傳記電影《黃金時代》（2014）等。
講座報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741319

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

Your Voice Matters – International Study on Discrimination in Higher Education
We warmly invite you to participate in an important global research study exploring the experiences and impact of discrimination in higher education institutions worldwide.
An international consortium of 52 higher education institutions from 20 countries, in collaboration with Federation University Australia, is conducting this study. It aims to better understand how discrimination — whether based on race, gender, age, disability, religion, appearance, or other characteristics — affects the wellbeing, sense of belonging, and success of both staff and students.
Who can participate?
If you are
18 years or older
and currently working or studying at a higher education institution, we would love to hear from you.
The survey is
completely anonymous and voluntary
, and it takes only about
25 minutes
to complete. Your honest experiences will help shape more inclusive, respectful, and culturally safe environments in universities across the globe.
To participate, simply click the link:
https://federation.syd1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_79VUajkBSaR8TVs

, The Nethersole School of Nursing, CUHK.

CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project
Funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project (“
the Project
”) brings together the strong expertise of CUHK Faculties of Engineering and Education. The Project’s objective is to create a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) curriculum, a sustainable AI education model, with relevant supporting infrastructure to establish a conducive ecosystem in AI education for Hong Kong’s secondary schools.
About Toolkit Team
To facilitate teachers’ teaching and students’ learning AI, the Toolkit Team is responsible for developing AI toolkits to support the Project’s AI Curriculum. The Toolkit team is also responsible for managing the Project’s AI Education and Exploration Lab (“the Lab”) at CUHK, as well as to develop AI-related demonstrations to be exhibited at the Lab and offer AI educational activities such as workshops and courses.
The Project team is looking for part-time students focusing on
web application
. Job responsibilities and requirements are as follows:
No. of Vacancies:
5
Salary:
HKD 67 per hour
Working Hours:
A minimum of 4 hours/ week and maximum 17 hours/ week
(Basically onsite working, unless otherwise subject to University announcement of pandemic work arrangement)
Working Location:
Rm 902, 9/F, William M. W. Mong Engineering Building (ERB), CUHK
OR
HKSTP
Job Descriptions
To assist in developing web applications related to AI education and AI toolkits;
To work with designers to develop websites’ user interface;
To conduct research and experiments on web technologies and frameworks;
To document code and maintain code repositories; and
To handle any ad hoc duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Study Year Requirements
Full-time undergraduate students
Full-time postgraduate students
Other Requirements
Basic knowledge of JavaScript/ HTML/ CSS;
Basic knowledge of using Git for project version management;
Experience in front-end development, particularly responsive web design/UI/UX design would be a plus;
Possess a good track record in technical development; and
Responsible, willingness to learn and able to work independently.
(Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview)
Please submit your CV and state the position(s) that you want to apply by email to Miss. Rachel CHEN (rachelchen@cuhk.edu.hk) by 23:59, 18 Oct 2026 (Sun).

Dear all,
We warmly invite you to a book talk celebrating the launch of Professor Susanne Choi's new book,
Queer Resistance: Contesting State, Family, and Inequality in Post-Socialist China
.
Drawing on a decade of research, the book explores how LGBTQ+ individuals in post-socialist China navigate state governance, family expectations, gender norms, and social inequalities while seeking intimacy, dignity, and belonging.

Announcements
*Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email:
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: 香港中文大學普通話教育研究及發展中心

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
推廣普通話計劃：普通話語匯通 2026/27
本計劃由語文教育及研究常務委員會（語常會）支持、語文基金撥款

面向本港小四至小六學生，免費參加。
旨在強化並深化學生對普通話語匯的認識，幫助學生把握語匯的語義，感悟其背後的文化底蘊。在創設的情境中，提高學生運用普通話語匯水平，進行有效的口語交際。
2026/27
學年的活動加入全新內容。大部分活動將於香港中文大學校園舉行。
每月設不同活動，包括：講座、親子工作坊、自學活動、參訪活動、情境對話等。
最新活動：
語匯大講堂（一）構詞

普通話水平測試應試證書課程（

）（持續進修基金課程編號：38C155714
）
中文大學校園面授
本證書課程以參加國家語委普通話水平測試（PSC）為導向，旨在提高學員普通話應用水平，具體表現為：提高學員普通話朗讀能力，掌握普通話水平測試常用詞匯，掌握朗讀規定篇目的方法，讀準字音，讀通作品。同時，提高學員使用普通話所達到的流利程度和規範程度，掌握普通話水平測試應試的技巧，做好測試前的準備；並幫助參加過測試的應試人進一步提升等級，説話時，逐步做到語音標準，語調自然，表達流暢。本證書課程不是零起點課程，學員須具有基礎普通話能力。

2026

月）

‼~ ( Maximum $5⃣0⃣0⃣allowance!) Recruiting youths (aged 15–24) for online self-help mental health treatment study ~‼ ‼~誠邀15至24歲青年參加網上自助心理健康療程研究（最高可獲得$5⃣0⃣0⃣津貼！） ~‼ - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式網上自助心理健康療程對改善青年睡眠及情緒健康的成效。現招募年齡介乎15歲至24歲青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 15歲至24歲青年
2. 有失眠及情緒症狀
3. 過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
參與為期6週的手機App自助療程
每週觀看20分鐘左右的網上療程
完成四次網上問卷及七天睡眠日記，包括治療前、治療後、三個月跟進及六個月跟進
全部評估及治療皆在電話或網上進行，無需面見！
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 黃小姐)查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of an online self-help mobile app program for improving sleep and emotional well-being among youths. We would like to invite participants aged between 15 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Youths aged between 15-24 years
2. Experience symptoms of insomnia and emotional distress
3. Have not received psychological or medication treatment for these issues in the past 3 months
What will you do?
Join a 6-week self-help treatment via mobile app
Attend 20 minutes of online therapy weekly
Complete four online surveys and seven-day sleep diary: before treatment, after treatment, at 3-month follow-up, and at 6-month follow-up during the study
All assessments and treatments are conducted via phone or online — no in-person visits required!
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 Miss Wong).

title: We need you!! AI+Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research 一齊聽歌！!AI+Music!! 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
bodyText:

Announcements
We need you!! AI+Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research 一齊聽歌！!AI+Music!! 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?

Announcements
We need you!! AI+Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research 一齊聽歌！!AI+Music!! 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

Announcements
Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500  「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.

From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

朋輩支援網絡2027成員招募 ── 現正接受報名！
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心致力推動朋輩支援，透過凝聚一群熱心的本科生，並安排相關的培訓及服務機會，裝備他們服務中大學生社群。朋輩支援網絡 (Peer Support Network - PSN) 2027的三組團隊現正接受報名！如果你是香港中文大學全日制非畢業班本科生，樂於助人並充滿熱誠，我們非常歡迎你加入PSN。
uBuddies朋輩輔導聯網（主要以廣東話進行）
uBuddies朋輩輔導聯網致力在校園內推廣關顧文化，宣揚朋輩互助的精神。透過一連串有系統的培訓及籌辦多個有意義的服務項目，uBuddies將掌握有效的朋輩輔導技巧，為朋輩提供情緒支援及推廣心理健康，並能促進個人成長，增強自信和發揮個人潛能。所有訓練將主要以廣東話進行。
uShine特殊教育需要服務隊（主要以廣東話進行）
uShine特殊教育需要服務隊旨在為有特殊教育需要（SEN）的學生在大學生活適應上提供適切的支援，並透過推行不同活動，提升校內人士對特殊教育需要的認識和了解，同建共融校園。所有訓練將主要以廣東話進行。
uPals心理健康推廣團隊（以英語進行）
為連結中大多元化及國際化的學生社群，中心於2020年成立了uPals心理健康推廣團隊。uPals各項培訓及服務項目均以英語進行，提供多姿多彩及促進共融的活動。
如果你希望在中大校園內推廣心理健康，籌辦豐富的活動和建立深刻的友誼，就立即申請你感興趣的PSN計劃啦！我們期待在PSN的大家庭裡和你結伴同行！

Recruitment of Peer Support Network 2027 – Join Us Now!
The Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs endeavours to enhance students’ peer support through engaging dedicated students, providing them with relevant training and service opportunities and empowering them to serve CUHK students. The following three teams under the Peer Support Network (PSN) 2027 are now open for applications! Don’t miss the chance and submit your application now!
uBuddies Peer Counselling Network (conducted mainly in Cantonese)
The uBuddies Peer Counselling Network aims to promote a caring culture on campus and foster the spirit of peer support. Through intensive training and services which help enhancing personal growth and realizing their potential, uBuddies will be well equipped to provide peer counselling and organise a range of meaningful service projects on campus. All training will be mainly conducted in Cantonese.
uShine SEN Service Team (conducted mainly in Cantonese)
The uShine SEN Service Team focuses on facilitating peers with special educational needs (SEN) in the adjustment of campus life while raising awareness and understanding of SEN among the CUHK community, thus fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment. All training will be mainly conducted in Cantonese.
uPals Wellness Promotion Team (conducted in English)
Recognising the needs of non-local students, WACC launched the uPals Wellness Promotion Team in 2020. uPals are trained and operate entirely in English, offering vibrant and inclusive wellness activities that connect and support CUHK’s diverse and international student community.
If you wish to promote mental wellness, organise various activities and build meaningful connections at CUHK, apply for the programme that resonates with you now! Join us and thrive together in the PSN family!
Learn More about PSN:
https://wacc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/wellness-programme/peer-support-network/

Recruitment of Peer Support Network 2027 – Join Us Now!
The Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs endeavours to enhance students’ peer support through engaging dedicated students, providing them with relevant training and service opportunities and empowering them to serve CUHK students. The following three teams under the Peer Support Network (PSN) 2027 are now open for applications! Don’t miss the chance and submit your application now!
uBuddies Peer Counselling Network (conducted mainly in Cantonese)
The uBuddies Peer Counselling Network aims to promote a caring culture on campus and foster the spirit of peer support. Through intensive training and services which help enhancing personal growth and realizing their potential, uBuddies will be well equipped to provide peer counselling and organise a range of meaningful service projects on campus. All training will be mainly conducted in Cantonese.
uShine SEN Service Team (conducted mainly in Cantonese)
The uShine SEN Service Team focuses on facilitating peers with special educational needs (SEN) in the adjustment of campus life while raising awareness and understanding of SEN among the CUHK community, thus fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment. All training will be mainly conducted in Cantonese.
uPals Wellness Promotion Team (conducted in English)
Recognising the needs of non-local students, WACC launched the uPals Wellness Promotion Team in 2020. uPals are trained and operate entirely in English, offering vibrant and inclusive wellness activities that connect and support CUHK’s diverse and international student community.
If you wish to promote mental wellness, organise various activities and build meaningful connections at CUHK, apply for the programme that resonates with you now! Join us and thrive together in the PSN family!

title: HK$300Brain Health Study 💰💰HK$300💰中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究🧠
bodyText:

2026/09/18
»
Announcements
HK$300Brain Health Study  💰💰HK$300💰中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究🧠 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)

Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:

Android users:

From: Maggie Lee

2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!

香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！

如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.

free of charge
and on a
first-come-first-served
basis.
Eligibility: Patients aged 4 to 17 years with atopic dermatitis and who meet the screening criteria.

The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care would like to recruit full-time students who are able to understand Cantonese to help with editing Chinese subtitles of videos of lectures, conducted in Cantonese, of a professional continuing education course for local registered Chinese Medicine Practitioners.  Please find more details in Chinese as follows:
賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院現正招募有興趣的同學為一個本地註冊中醫師修讀的專業進修課程（以粵語授課）之影片編輯中文字幕。詳情如下：
日期：       由現時至 12月上旬 ，按同學自身時間表而編排工作時間
工作地點：遙距工作，唯需出席首次會面及工作簡介
首次會面地點：沙田威爾斯醫院中文大學賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院（從港鐡第一城站步行約10分鐘距離。地圖地址：
https://maps.app.goo.gl/ek2XfXAKCR3wBoba8
)
要求：        1) 現為中文大學全日制學生
2) 懂粵語，母語為粵語為佳 (因講者的語速較快)
3) 懂中文輸入法
4) 富有耐性、小心
課堂的主題涵蓋基層醫療及家庭醫學之知識及應用，中醫及西醫文獻，醫療制度、管理及倫理法律，基礎輔導及衝突處理。主修中醫藥學，或對以上課題有興趣的同學將更投入工作。

lyou@cuhk.edu.hk

title: [Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free 6-week Online Treatment Study 【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡

Announcements
[Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free 6-week Online Treatment Study 【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡 - Department of psychiatry
From: Reyane Ao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您是否正飽受
惡夢
與
失眠
的雙重困擾，覺得身心俱疲？
反覆的惡夢有機會加劇失眠問題，導致日頭精神大打折扣。
我們誠邀您參與一項
【網上認知行為療法治療噩夢與失眠共病】臨床研究
。本研究旨在評估一項手機應用程式的自助式網上療程，學習有效改善睡眠、減少惡夢的心理療法。
您的參與不僅有機會能幫助自己重獲優質睡眠，更能推動睡眠醫學的發展，為有同樣困擾的人士帶來新的證據。

我們正在招募
年齡介乎 18 至 64 歲
同時受失眠及惡夢問題困擾
能閱讀繁體中文並以粵語溝通

研究內容包括
臨床訪談及問卷篩查
為期6周網上認知行為治療課程（每週約20-30分鐘課程）
完成治療後的問卷和跟進評估
佩戴睡眠手錶

參與方法
如有興趣，請點擊以下連結，花1-2分鐘填寫篩選問卷：

title: Story of Chinese Ink in the Mountain Town – Boneless Painting Programme 「山城墨語」水墨課程（沒骨畫篇）

Story of Chinese Ink in the Mountain Town – Boneless Painting Programme 「山城墨語」水墨課程（沒骨畫篇） - New Asia College
From: New Asia College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
nac@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「沒骨法」是中國畫的傳統技法之一，有別於一般以輪廓勾勒為主的方式，它強調以暈染、設色與用墨等技巧塑造形象，不以線條框限物象，富有表現力。此技法不僅可應用於花鳥、山水、人物等多元的題材，更能呈現細膩工緻到瀟灑寫意的多樣風格。
本課程以花鳥題材及歷代名家畫作為核心，系統性地講授沒骨畫的基本技法，並引導學員逐步探索個人的創作語彙，發展出個人化的藝術風格。除常見的掛軸與壓鏡裝裱形式外，課程亦將介紹冊頁、長卷等不同裝幀方式，拓展學員對作品呈現形式的理解。為豐富學習視野，課程特別邀請不同藝術家與講者，分享中國水墨藝術不同面貌的風格和技巧。完成課程後，學員將共同參與及策劃展覽，完整展示學習成果。
歡迎所有中大本科生及教職員（新亞學生優先）！
>>
課程詳細內容
網上報名
(
截止日期：
2026年9月27日)
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741106
查詢：新亞輔導處楊先生 (
jasonyeung@cuhk.edu.hk
/ 39437612) 或王先生 (
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
/ 39431690)
The “boneless method” is one of the traditional techniques of Chinese painting. Unlike the common approach that relies on outlined contours, this technique emphasizes the use of dyeing, colour application and ink work to shape forms. It makes the subject highly expressive without confining with lines. This method can be applied to a wide range of genres, including birds-and-flowers, landscapes, and figures, and can achieve styles that vary from finely detailed and delicate to freely expressive and spirited.
This course centers on the birds-and-flowers genre and the masterpieces by renowned Chinese painters, offering systematic instruction in the fundamental techniques of boneless painting. Students will be guided to gradually explore their own creative vocabulary and develop their own distinctive artistic style. In addition to common presentation formats such as hanging scrolls and framed glass-mounted pieces, the course will also introduce various mounting styles including album leaves and handscrolls, broadening students’ understanding of how finished works can be presented. To enrich the learning experience, the course will invite various artists and speakers to share their perspectives on different stylistic approaches and techniques found across Chinese painting traditions. Upon completion of the course, students will collaborate in planning and organizing an exhibition, showcasing the outcomes of their learning journey.
All CUHK undergraduates and full-time staff members are welcome (Priority for New Asia students)!

bodyText:

Midday Oasis: Solo Handpan Concert , Sasah Frolov   「午間心靈綠洲」:手碟獨奏音樂會 Sasah Frolov - Chaplain's Office, Chung Chi College
From: Chaplain's Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chaplaincy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「午間心靈綠洲」
為大家預備一場為心靈而演奏的手碟音樂會。
有一種聲音，不急於到達。
它同時承載節奏、旋律與和聲，卻不把人往前推，只把時間慢慢鋪開。聽的時候，外面的節奏會暫時退下，呼吸會自己回來。
手碟演奏家Sasha Frolov 是香港少數專業手碟演奏者之一。他的樂音不像表演更像一個空間：平靜、有共鳴，帶著一種安靜的陪伴。他同樣看重技巧與心靈的連結，希望人聽見自己與音樂之間的對話。
Sasha由非洲鼓 Djembe 的原始脈搏開始，後來被手碟那種罕見的完整深深吸引——從此，音樂對他不再只是演奏，而是一場向內走、又向外展開的旅程。
這場音樂會，邀請你暫時放下理解與反應。
只要來，坐下來，讓聲音自己到來。
“Midday Oasis” -  A Handpan concert for the soul.
There is a kind of sound that does not hurry to arrive.
It holds rhythm, melody and harmony at once, yet it does not push us forward. It only opens time, slowly. As we listen, the outer pace recedes, and the breath returns on its own.
Handpan artist Sasha Frolov is one of Hong Kong’s few professional handpan players. His sound is less a performance than a space: still, resonant, quietly companionable. He also holds both craft and spirit, hoping that others may hear the conversation between themselves and the music.
Sasha’s path began with the raw pulse of the African djembe; later he was drawn deeply by the rare completeness of the handpan.
From then on, music was no longer only performance for him, but a journey that moves both inward and outward.
This concert invites you to set aside, for a while, the need to understand or respond.
Just come. Sit down. Let the sound arrive.

creative
and

role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).

and

An online mental health course study for individuals with depression or anxiety symptoms [Earn max. HKD280] 誠邀正經歷抑鬱或焦慮症狀的人士參與網上心理健康課程研究 [最高可獲港幣$280答謝金！] - Psychology
From: Alan Tong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
網上心理健康課程研究

參加者招募

我們誠摯邀請你參與心理學系的一項研究，旨在更深入了解網上心理健康課程提供的不同內容如何影響使用者的參與度。這項研究為期大約四個月，期間你將獲邀填寫5份網上問卷，每份約需10分鐘完成。為感謝你的寶貴時間和投入，你最多可獲得總值港幣280元現金券作為回饋。你的回應對我們日後的服務優化極為重要。

我們正在招募能夠滿足以下條件的參加者：
年滿十八歲
能使用互聯網
懂得使用電子設備（包括：電腦、手機或平板電腦）
能閱讀和理解中文或英文
正在經歷抑鬱或焦慮症狀，且困擾持續2個月。（由研究人員篩選評估）
在過去三個月內未曾參與賽馬會心導遊+平台上的認知行為課程（針對抑鬱焦慮情緒）及其相關研究項目

參與研究，你將會：
完成篩查調查確認參加資格
*
完成前測問卷（需時大約10分鐘）
在6星期內完成8個單元的網上心理健康課程
每完成一個單元後，參加者將會透過他們的電郵及平台郵箱獲得相應的文字反饋，及填寫簡短單元問卷（約3分鐘）
在完成整個課程，完成課程後的一個月及三個月後分別完成後測、跟進1及跟進2問卷
參加者將會被隨機分派到三組：實驗組1、實驗組2或對照組，並獲得一個網上心理健康平台的帳戶進行本研究設計的課程。參加者需要在其後的6星期研究期間
每星期登入平台至少兩次、且每次花大約
15
分鐘完成學習一個單元（總共
8
個單元）
。
 為答謝你所付出的時間，在研究完成後你最高可獲得總值港幣
280
元
現金券#！
*
由於名額有限，若果報名人數過多，將會隨機抽取部分合資格人士參與研究，問卷將透過電郵發送，並需要在收到後的四日內完成。
#
經實驗驗人員確認後，現金券會分三次在完成
跟進
2
問卷後
3
個月內
派發。
如你對此項研究感興趣，請立即點擊以下連結或掃描QR code了解詳情並報名登記！
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_5d2mVuE84SVimk6
本研究已獲得香港中文大學調查及行為研究倫理委員會 (編號：SBRE‐24‐0541)。
Study on Online Mental Health Course
 Recruitment of Participants
We’re reaching out to invite you to join an important study conducted by the Department of Psychology, to better understand how different elements in online mental health courses influence user engagement. The study will last for approximately four months, during which you will be asked to complete 5 online questionnaires, each taking about 10 minutes. To thank you for your valuable time and effort, you can receive up to HK$280 in cash vouchers. Your responses are crucial for our current services’ future improvement.
The study is looking for
:
Aged 18 or above
Able to access the internet
Able to use electronic devices (e.g., computers, smartphones, or tablets)

各位︰
「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，兩場知識與美學兼具的專題講座將於10 月 25 日（日）及11 月 28 日（六）在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行。
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。
本講座系列為香港研究資助局協作研究計劃「嶺南文化與世界」項目（2023–2026）活動，亦是弘揚中華文化系列的活動之一。

*

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries, features two insightful talks exploring the aesthetic side of Lingnan.  Two lectures will be held at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 25 October (Sunday) and 28 November (Saturday).
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

From: Whitney Sia

各位︰
「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，兩場知識與美學兼具的專題講座將於10 月 25 日（日）及11 月 28 日（六）在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行。
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。
本講座系列為香港研究資助局協作研究計劃「嶺南文化與世界」項目（2023–2026）活動，亦是弘揚中華文化系列的活動之一。

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries, features two insightful talks exploring the aesthetic side of Lingnan.  Two lectures will be held at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 25 October (Sunday) and 28 November (Saturday).
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

你想了解孩子對於學校或日常生活裡的“領導”的看法嗎？想知道孩子對於“當領導”的意願嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會。簡單進行線上研究，還有報酬可領喔~~
招募對象
：
在香港就讀小1到小6的小學生以及其父親或母親
目前各個組別依舊在積極招募，尤其小2、小5、小6組別以及各個組別的女孩子組依舊席位多多！誠摯邀請合乎要求的小朋友同家長參與~~如果你們身邊有合乎要求的小朋友和家長，也懇請幫我們多多宣傳~~
研究項目：
小學生、家長及老師的領導認知與刻板印象
研究內容（全程以中文進行）：
1.孩子：1對1線上訪談（需錄音），約需1小時。
2.家長：填寫1份網上問卷，約需1小時。
報酬：
家長和孩子完成各自的研究項目後，可獲得共100港幣報酬。
參與條件：
1.兒童參加者為在港就讀小1到小6的小學生，家長參加者為該兒童的父親或母親。
2.兒童能講流利廣東話或普通話，家長能閱讀和書寫中文。
3.兒童可使用有互聯網、視頻和音頻功能的電腦或平板參與研究。
4.兒童沒有主要的身體障礙（如：視障、四肢不健全）和未被診斷有任何有關精神健康或主要的發展障礙的狀況（如：自閉症、過度活躍）。
5.請留意參加者需在此前沒有參與過本研究的“預實驗”或“教師部分”（如不清楚是否參與過也可先留下聯繫方式，稍後我們的研究人員將與您聯繫進行確認）。
如對本實驗感興趣，請通過以下鏈接報名
，我們的研究人員將盡快聯繫您：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KzWB6HhTtOhwou
參與純屬自願性質，所收集的資料只作研究用途及保密處理。如有任何疑問，請聯繫何小姐（conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk)。

From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15
分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
*
現在報名的幼稚園高班至六年級學童只需完成今年一次測試
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：今年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。
We are recruiting for a multi-disciplinary study about the Chinese, English, and Mathematical abilities among Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong. Details are as below:
Target participants:
Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2025/26 school year
Students’ parents
The child participant must be a native Cantonese speaker and have lived in Hong Kong for more than 2.5 years.
Content:
Part 1
Students
: A series of assessments on Chinese, English, and mathematics on the project’s online testing platform. The tasks are divided into six portions; each takes about 40 minutes to finish. Online testing can be completed at your own pace, as long as all tasks are completed within 4 weeks.
A follow-up face-to-face session (45 minutes) will be arranged upon completion of the online testing.
Parents
: Short online testing on language and mathematics abilities (15 minutes), as well as a set of questionnaires on children’s learning and home language environment
*For current registration
s, students from K3 to P6 only need to complete the test once this year.
Part 2 (optional)
Students: electroencephalography (EEG) test (~2 hour)
Rewards: After each round of testing, participants will receive:
(1) Personal performance report; (2) $200 supermarket vouchers; (3) a gift (for students); EEG participants will receive an additional $250 worth of supermarket vouchers
The details of the study and the registration form can be found in the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
Should you have any enquiries, please contact Prof. Urs Maurer, the principle investigator (umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk) or the research team (3943-4379 or lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com).

教育心理學系謝志成教授一項關於中文複合詞的研究誠意邀請與會者參與。
對象：
**參加者需為粵語是母語的本港學生；
**參與者需要有良好的視力或矯正視力；
**參與者需慣性用右手。
**參與者年齡需大於18嵗。
研究內容：整個實驗將為期三節（每節之間間隔不超過一星期）進行，每節需要 1 至 1.5 小
時，完成3節後可得到250港元作為現金補償。
地點：陳國本樓707E室
參
與方式：如有興趣，請點此連結報名https://forms.gle/znR7QB79PVof2F87A
（報名時個人資料包括：姓名、學號、性別、年齡、學系、年級、聯絡電話、聯絡電郵。）
有興趣的同學請提供每週至少兩個時間段，以便安排。
*若閣下沒有收到我們的電郵，代表所選的時間已額滿，多謝！
*若已參加過【對於中文複合詞所表達的情感】的研究，請勿重複報名。
