Invitation to ICS Public Lecture – Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee on 24 September 2026 誠邀參加中國文化研究所訪問學人公開講座──李晉美博士（芝加哥藝術學院） - Institute of Chinese Studies
From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 24 September 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. From: Amber Lam
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 24 September 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

From: Donald Liu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：10月尾開始 星期三或四的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。
如需了解更多本研究資訊或查詢，請聯絡：
廖先生/魏先生 (研究助理)
電話：2252-8463  Whatsapp: 5264 6865
如有興趣參與研究，請使用以下連結報名。

The Chinese version follows the English version of this email.
Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to June 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).

Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/11
»
Announcements
(Earn $700!!!) Recruiting adults aged 18–65 who have recovered from depression to participate in a study on depression recurrence (participants on medication are welcome if condition is medically stable) (獲得 $700!!!) 誠邀年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與預測抑鬱症復發相關的研究(歡迎仍在服藥但病情穩定者參加) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，探討運用語音分析能否預測抑鬱症復發。現招募年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與研究。詳情如下：
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者
廣東話為母語
使用智慧型手機並可持續連接互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
接受臨床評估作為篩查
填寫問卷
連續
7
天
於指定的手機應用程式以語音方式記錄情緒狀態
一年後接受跟進臨床評估
完成整個實驗及跟進評估，可以獲得最多HK$700作為研究津貼
如有興趣參與研究，請按以下連結填寫篩選問卷。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
若您適合參與研究，研究人員會聯絡您解釋研究詳情。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
If you are interested, please complete the following screening questionnaire.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
If you are suitable for participating in the study, the researchers will contact you to explain the study details.
Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Phoebe Chan

mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題

Major in psychology or related disciplines
Highly motivated

香港中文大學體育運動科學系運動營養與體力活動實驗室
誠邀您參加一項運動幹預研究!本研究將有助於瞭解您的運動代謝表現並提高您的代謝健康。
研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。
平時運動較少（每星期少於 150 分鐘中等強度體能活動、少於 75 分鐘劇烈強度體能活動，或二者同等組合）。
過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。
⏳
您需要做什麼？（
3
次評估
+ 12
周幹預訓練）
本研究為期 12 週，合格者將隨機分配至對照組、有氧運動組A、有氧運動組B，期間需前往香港中文大學實驗室進行 3 次評估，具體包括：問卷調查、空腹靜脈抽血檢測、指尖採血、身體成分測量、運動代謝測試。為減少測試過程中的不適感，運動代謝測試將與其他健康測試分開進行，整個研究過程中，您總共需要到達實驗室

Invitation to Participate in CUHK Health Study: Free 12-Week Exercise Guidance and
Comprehensive Health Check!
(Complete the trial and receive a HK$150 shopping voucher)
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Exercise Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory
Sender: He Wenke
For any questions, please contact:
wenke.he@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Exercise Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Overweight or Obese Postmenopausal Women
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in overweight or obese postmenopausal women. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).
3. Are usually physically inactive (less than 150 minutes of moderate‑intensity physical activity, less than 75 minutes of vigorous‑intensity physical activity per week, or an equivalent combination).
4. Have had relatively stable body weight in the past 3 months, and have no serious contraindications to exercise (e.g., severe heart disease, stroke, etc.).
⏳ What do you need to do? (3 assessments + 12‑week intervention training)
This study lasts 12 weeks. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a
control group
,
aerobic
exercise group A,
or
aerobic exercise group B
. During the period, you will need to visit the laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong for 3 assessments, including: questionnaire surveys, fasting venous blood draw, finger‑prick blood sampling, body composition measurement, and exercise metabolic testing. To reduce discomfort during testing, the exercise metabolic test will be conducted separately from other health tests. Throughout the study, you will need to come to the laboratory
6 times.
12‑week intervention training: 3 times per week, 40‑70 minutes each session, for 12 weeks.
Upon completion of the study, you will receive a HK$150 shopping voucher and a health report.
Trial location: G02 Office, Ground Floor, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Register now / Enquire:
Places are limited, first‑come, first‑served! You can click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfZKjSc55Ov13iAjw_GAGkFIbINsXc9rH1ePEYg6CWrU5w5Ew/viewform?usp=header
If you have any questions, please contact the research team:
Study coordinator: Ms. He (WhatsApp: +852 5984 8824)
Supervising professor: Professor Wang Xiangsheng (Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wishing you good health!
Research Team
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Respectfully

Announcements
Research Participant Recruitment: Chinese Adult Reading Ability Assessment  - Psychology
From: Hui Wang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155232035@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
研究目的：
研發一份專屬漢語母語者群體的閱讀能力評估量表。
招募對象：
年齡18歲以上；
母語為粵語；
心理學或語言學背景亦可參與。
實驗資訊：
實驗地點：香港中文大學信和樓323室
實驗時長：60-90分鐘
實驗內容：紙筆語言測驗和問卷填寫。
參與回饋：
100 HKD 作為酬謝
感興趣的參與者可掃描海報上的QR Code或點擊下方連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScAJRZ13jq65jueJYiRoWbWsQebmL_uk1yeQjTqgsyqopUU-w/viewform?usp=header
參加者於網上登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，所有資料將會保密。若您符合參與要求，實驗人員將在隨後通過WhatsApp或電郵主動聯絡您跟進。如您對實驗有任何疑問，請聯絡王女士（WhatsApp/Phone: 61971099或Email: jingjinglab92@gmail.com ）。
Research Purpose:
To develop a reading ability assessment scale tailored for native Chinese speakers.
Recruitment Criteria:
Aged 18 or above;
Native Cantonese speakers;
Individuals with a background in psychology or linguistics are also welcome to participate.
Compensation & Benefits:
HK$100 honorarium;
Experiment Information:
Venue: In-person session at Room 323, Sino Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Duration: Approximately 60-90 minutes.
Procedure: Paper-and-pencil language tests and questionnaire completion.
Interested participants may scan the QR code on the poster or click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScAJRZ13jq65jueJYiRoWbWsQebmL_uk1yeQjTqgsyqopUU-w/viewform?usp=header
All personal information collected during online registration will be used exclusively for this study and handled with strict confidentiality. If you meet the participation requirements, our research team will follow up with you via WhatsApp or phone. For any inquiries, please contact Miss. Wang (WhatsApp/Phone: 61971099 or Email: jingjinglab92@gmail.com).
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

2026

9

28
日

或之前前往
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/TA/recruitment
填寫網上報名表，並上載相關文件（個人履歷表、學歷證明文件副本（如香港中學文憑試證書）等）。
申請人必須出席面試，成功通過面試的助教須出席相關培訓，藉此認識「資優計劃」的教育理念、資優生特質、以及處理課堂突發事情的技巧等。面試及培訓均在香港中文大學校園內舉辦，並以粵語進行。有關詳情請參閲海報或瀏覽

Recruitment of Part-time Teaching Assistant (Student Helper) for the Program for the Gifted and Talented, CUHK
The Program for the Gifted and Talented (PGT) at the Faculty of Education, CUHK, regularly offers Spring, Summer, and Winter enrichment programs for gifted students ranging from Primary 3 to Secondary 6. PGT is now inviting undergraduate or postgraduate students majoring in relevant disciplines to serve as part-time Teaching Assistants, supporting instructors’ teaching and assisting students’ learning. Teaching Assistant duties include taking attendance, distributing learning materials in class, facilitating students’ learning, classroom management, monitoring students’ learning progress, explaining lesson content to students in need or those with questions, planning and organising program events, assisting with promotion via PGT’s social media platforms, etc.
Undergraduate and postgraduate students who are interested in becoming Teaching Assistants for the Program for the Gifted and Talented are invited to complete the online application form at
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/TA/recruitment
and submit the required documents (Resume, Certificates of public examination results, etc.) by
28 September 2026 (Mon
).
Applicants must attend an interview. Successful candidates will be required to participate in a training session designed to enhance their understanding of the Program, the characteristics of gifted students, and classroom management techniques. Both the interview and the training will be conducted in Cantonese and held on the CUHK campus. Please refer to the attached Poster or visit
https://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/pgt/_Doc/TA_Recruitment/Leaflet_JoinTA.pdf
for details.
If you have any enquiries, please contact us at 2603-7444 or 2603-7485.

Announcements
Participants Needed for Chinese Word Rating Experiment (HK$60) 招募中文詞彙評分實驗參與者（報酬：港幣 $60) - Psychology
From: Yuxi Chen

1155187064@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Chinese Version
我們正進行一項關於中文詞彙的線上研究，現誠邀符合條件的人士參與。
實驗詳情
• 內容： 透過線上問卷（Qualtrics）對一系列中文雙字詞的詞彙特性進行評分。
• 所需時間： 約 45 至 50 分鐘（問卷不設時間限制，可按個人節奏完成）。
• 報酬： 完成問卷後可獲港幣 $60。

Dear all,
We cordially invite you to attend our upcoming
International Summit on Pain Research -
A CUHK and CUHK-Shenzhen Joint Forum
on
15 October 2026 (Thursday)
at Lecture Theatre 2, G/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA).
Featuring renowned speakers from the US, UK and Mainland China, the forum will delve into circuit mapping, neural mechanisms, and novel therapeutic opportunities in pain research.
In addition, emerging young researchers will share their latest findings and showcase cutting-edge translational research spanning microglial priming, hydrogel brain interfaces, and VR pain therapies.
For more details on the programme and speakers, please visit our website:
https://www.phpri.cuhk.edu.hk/news/peter_hung_pain_research_institute_international_summit_on_pain_research_cuhk_and_cuhk-shenzhen_joint_forum.html

香港中文大學學能提升研究中心現正招募二型糖尿病/前期糖尿患者參與
【基於自決理論的跨專業干預，以改善香港基層醫療機構的糖尿病管理】
研究計劃，目的旨在開發和驗證適合香港情況的跨專業教育干預措施，為政府的衛生保健策略提供資訊，以加强慢性病管理。

https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cNNsLtBwB2nxkR8
或掃描海報中的QR code填寫網上報名表，研究人員將會初步評估及聯絡合適的參加者。
如有查詢，請於星期一至五(公眾假期除外)辦公時間內致電3943 5015查詢。

Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research – CLEAR, The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting individuals with Type 2 diabetes mellitus to participate in a study
【
Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus
ma
nagement
】
.
It aims to examine the effects and mechanisms of a theory-based educational program on diabetes mellitus management and provide evidence for potential policy changes in the framework for care of diabetes mellitus in primary care settings.
If you are interested, please fill in the online form via
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cNNsLtBwB2nxkR8
or scan the QR code in the above poster. We will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study.
For inquiries, please contact us during office hour (Mon-Fri):  3943 5015.

From: BSc in Global Economics and Finance Programme
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
glef@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear CUHK non-final-year undergraduate students,
If you wish to apply to change your Major Programme to BSc in Global Economics and Finance (GLEF) in 27-28, please note that this ‘transfer-in’ application is on a competitive basis.
Academic Requirements
:
- Achieve good grades in at least 8 units from the following courses: DOTE1030 or ECON2011, DOTE1040 or ECON2021, ECON1101 or MATH1010/1510/1520, ECON1111.
- Other “equivalent” courses may be considered with discretion, such as FINA2310 for non-business students. However, DOTE1031, DOTE1035, ECON1010 are not accepted as substitutes for DOTE1030 or ECON2011.
- Year 1 applicants are prioritized while other applicants will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Shortlisting Threshold
: Cumulative GPA 3.3 or above (up to 26-27 T1), on a selective basis
Admission Requirements
: Cumulative GPA 3.5 or above (up to 26-27 T2) and strong interview performance, on a selective basis
Application Period
: 23 January (10am, Saturday) – 5 February (5pm, Friday), 2027 (HKT)
Application Method:
Submit online application form + submit supporting documents by email. Early submission is appreciated.
Interview Date
: During reading week (8-13 March 2027) (to be confirmed). Shortlisted applicants must attend the interview. No exceptions (e.g. Zoom interviews or any other forms of make-up interviews) will be granted.
Interview
F
ormat:
Face-to-face.
Other Details:
Refer to our website.
GLEF reserves the right to modify the information without prior notice. In the event of disputes, GLEF shall prevail. Always refer to our website for the most up-to-date and accurate information.
Best regards,
Global Economics and Finance Programme
Department of Economics & Department of Finance
https://cuhk.hk/glef

bodyText:

Announcements
Brief Guided Self-Help Training Programme for Eating Disorders and Self-Criticism 「饮食问题低强度心理治疗」诚邀普通话女性使用者 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募参与者：饮食问题低强度心理治疗
香港中文大学临床心理科学实验室团队现正推行一项针对饮食失调问题人群的短期训练计划，诚邀符合资格的人士参与。
六周指导式自助练习，处理与情绪和自我的关系
探索自我批评的恶性循环
开启看待自我的新视角
香港中文大学校园内，全程免费
饮食失调问题很多时候并非只是一个关于食物、身材偏好或者意志力的问题，而关乎我们如何看待自己，以及如何处理和他人的关系。目前，针对饮食失调的治疗多采用认知行为取向，研究证实能有效控制非适应性饮食失调行为的出现。本计划是团队基于实证研究开发的新训练方案，采用社会情绪取向，聚焦于处理自己与他人的关系。本项目遵循阶梯式照护模式，定位为指导式自助短期介入方案，旨在以较少的时间投入及心理负担为参加者提供支援。
训练为期6周，包括「每周1次实体会面 + 自助练习 + 线上心理评估访谈及问卷」；训练完成后1个月及6个月进行跟进评估。
「招募要求」
年满18岁或以上；女性；普通话流利（训练将主要使用普通话）；
受饮食失调问题困扰，例如，对饮食失调、体重或体型有过度的关注，饮食失调后感到强烈自责或羞愧，反复出现无法控制的暴食行为，或伴有反复出现的代偿行为（催吐、使用泻药或利尿剂、过度运动等）并因此影响日常生活或情绪；
目前并未接受其他形式的心理治疗或精神科药物治疗；
能够亲身前往香港中文大学校园参与训练。
「报名链接」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
报名后，我们将联络您安排筛选问卷及访谈，以确认是否适合参加本计划，并邀请符合条件者参与训练。
如有疑问请联络研究团队：epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk。
所有个人资料仅用作研究用途，并会严格保密。
临床心理科学实验室团队
Recruiting Participants: Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at CUHK is currently running a brief training programme for individuals struggling with eating disorders. We are now inviting eligible participants to join.
We all care about how we look. But eating disorders are often about much more than food, body shape, or willpower—they are deeply tied to how we see ourselves and how we relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) is the most widely used and evidence-based treatment for eating disorders, our team has developed a new training protocol grounded in recent research, drawing on a socioemotional framework that focuses specifically on self-perception and interpersonal relationships. Following a stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, offering meaningful support with a relatively low time commitment and psychological load.
  The programme runs for 6 weeks:
Weekly in-person sessions on campus
Guided self-help practice tasks to complete between sessions
Online assessment interviews and questionnaires
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted at 1 month and 6 months post-training.

Who We're Looking For
Female aged 18 or above;
Are fluent in Mandarin;
Are currently struggling with eating disorder symptoms, for example, excessive evaluation or concerns on food, weight, or body shape, intense guilt or shame after eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating that feel out of control, with compensatory behaviours such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, or excessive exercise;
Are not currently receiving any other form of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication;
Are able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus

Sign Up Here
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
After you sign up, we will contact you to complete a screening questionnaire and a brief interview to see if this programme is a good fit for you. If eligible, you will be invited to join the 6-week training.
 For any questions, feel free to reach out to us at:
epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research screening and intervention purposes.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory

For enquiries, please write to:

我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀， 且有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲，
無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：
一份認知能力測試報告
+
一份純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：
一份非語言智商測試報告
+
一份價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：現金
HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(
functional near-infrared spectroscopy
, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test)
report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200
allowance
and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!

Announcements
[Free of charge] [An allowance of up to HKD $1,000 will be provided upon successful enrollment] Recruitment of Diabetes Patients (Aged 18-80 years) for clinical trials of Chinese Medicine (Powder) Treatment 💰💰[費用全免] 📣[成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼] 🙋🏻招募年齡介於 18-70 歲的糖尿病人士- 中藥(沖劑)治療臨床研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365
View Count

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Two Educational Laptop & Tablet Offers Coming Your Way ⌨
Looking for a new computer or tablet for your teaching and studies?  The NOP Workgroup is pleased to introduce
two educational computing offers for CUHK staff and students
.
CUHK Student Notebook Ownership Program 2026
NOP 2026 features a broad selection of Windows PCs from ASUS, HP, and Lenovo, as well as computing accessories to support your learning and productivity.

Online store:
www.cuhk.edu.hk/event/nop
You can also visit the
Roadshow
to explore selected products in person:

7 - 14 September 2026

Multi-purpose Hall (Room G01), Pommerenke Student Centre
Apple MacBook and iPad Learning Offer
An educational offer featuring Apple MacBooks and iPads will also be available.
A dedicated online platform will be launched soon, with product information and ordering details to follow.
Please stay tuned for the upcoming announcement.

⭐⭐[Student Helper Recruitment] Chinese Language and Culture Experience Activities | Cross-cultural Exchange 【學生助理招募】中國語言文化體驗活動｜跨文化交流 - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【學生助理招募】中國語言文化體驗活動｜跨文化交流
雅禮中國語文研習所將於本學期舉辦一系列面向國際學生的中國語言文化體驗活動，主題涵蓋漢字與書法、傳統節慶、手工文化體驗、中文詩歌與文化分享。現誠邀中大學生擔任學生助理，協助活動籌備與現場支援。
活動時間：逢星期五下午，每次兩小時，預計本學期共舉辦5至6次
活動地點：方潤華堂（東鐵線大學站D出口對面）
申請條件：
對跨文化交流充滿熱情，性格開朗，具備良好英語溝通能力，並能說標準普通話或粵語；
具備與中華文化相關的才藝，如書法、茶藝，並樂意與國際學生交流分享；
喜歡華語電影、戲劇配音；
了解中文歌曲和古詩詞；
熟悉Gen-AI工具、Vide-Coding等，能使用Kahoot設計小遊戲;
能協助外出、深圳的參觀和導賞工作；
會編製中國結或印章雕刻的學生獲優先考慮
[SL1]
待遇：時薪 HKD$67 + 5% MPF
總工作時數：約15小時
有意者請於9月21日前填妥以下表格，合則約見：

報名表格
如有疑問，請聯絡陳小姐：
liyuanchen@cuhk.edu.hk
[Student Helper Recruitment] Chinese Language and Culture Experience Activities | Cross-cultural Exchange
The Yale-China Chinese Language Academy will host a series of cultural workshops this semester for international students, focusing on themes in Chinese language and culture, including Chinese characters, calligraphy, traditional festivals, handicrafts, poetry, songs, and cultural sharing. We are now recruiting CUHK students to assist with planning and running these events.
Schedule: Friday afternoons, 2 hours per session, approximately 5–6 sessions throughout the semester
Venue: Fong Yun Wah Hall (opposite University Station Exit D)
Requirements:
Passionate about cross-cultural communication, outgoing, fluent in English, and able to speak Putonghua or Cantonese;
Possess talents or skills related to Chinese culture and be willing to share and interact with international students;
Interest in Chinese film and drama dubbing;
Familiar with Chinese songs and classical poetry;
Experience with Gen-AI tools, Vide-Coding, and Kahoot for designing mini-games
Capable of assisting with outings, Chinese mainland visits, and guided tour services.
Priority will be given to students with skills in Chinese knot-making and Chinese seal carving.
[SL2]
Compensation: HKD$67/hr + 5% MPF
Total working hours: Around 15 hours
Interested applicants should complete the form below by September 21. Interviews will be arranged for shortlisted candidates:

Application Form
For inquiries, please contact Miss Chen at
liyuanchen@cuhk.edu.hk

各位︰
為紀念國學大師饒宗頤教授（1917–2018）誕辰一百一十週年，香港中文大學中國文化研究所聯合香港大學饒宗頤學術館、香港浸會大學饒宗頤國學院、香港大學馮平山圖書館和學海書樓共同舉辦「饒宗頤教授紀念講座系列」。九月至十月上旬之三場「頤學映真」專題講座由中國文化研究所主辦，將於9月12日、9 月19日及10月3日在香港中文大學舉行，特邀熟悉饒教授生平與學術成就的專家學者，從宗教史、考古學、書畫藝術等不同領域與視角，回顧、探討其學術貢獻與創見。

title: Join Woo Sing Choir! Auditions Now Open for Lee Woo Sing College & CUHK Students 202627 和聲合唱團2026-27年度團員招募｜歡迎和聲書院及中大學生報名參與試音！
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
Join Woo Sing Choir! Auditions Now Open for Lee Woo Sing College & CUHK Students 202627 和聲合唱團2026-27年度團員招募｜歡迎和聲書院及中大學生報名參與試音！ - Lee Woo Sing College
From: Fung Hoi Kuen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
henryfung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
和聲合唱團
現正展開2026-27年度成員招新！
我們誠摯邀請各位和聲同學及中大同學參與試音，成為和聲合唱團的一份子，令和諧之聲匯聚一堂。
和聲合唱團於2012年2月正式成立，即將迎來成立15週年。合唱團每年約有40至50名團員，是大學其中一個歷史悠久、規模最大的學生合唱團。團員每週於和聲音樂中心進行訓練，並積極參與書院高桌晚宴、迎新活動及不同典禮的演出。為展現團員一整年的學習成果，合唱團於每年下學期舉辦年度音樂會，與大學成員分享精彩的音樂演出。團員來自不同背景，包括本地生、內地生及國際生，大家各展所長，以歌手或樂手的身分一同演出，攜手組成和諧共融的音樂大家庭。
無論你是專業的歌者，又或只是對唱歌抱有熱愛之心，和聲合唱團都真誠地歡迎你，供你在活動中提升音樂水平，在台前表演，以及結交到學園中志同道合、一同熱愛歌唱的好友知音。
試音時間：
第一節：8月25日 (二) 下午1:00-2:30
第二節：9月8日 (二) 下午1:00-2:30
第三節：9月10日 (四) 晚上6:30-8:00
地點：和聲書院音樂中心（和聲書院南座地下G04室）
試音報名表格 (
需登入)
：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737334
如欲了解和聲合唱團的詳情及過往演出，歡迎瀏覽以下合唱團的網頁：
https://www.ws.cuhk.edu.hk/ws-choir/
如對和聲合唱團或試音活動有任何疑問，歡迎透過電郵聯絡我們 (
wscollege@cuhk.edu.hk
)。
誠摯期待各位成為和聲合唱團的一份子！
We are pleased to announce that the
“Woo Sing Choir (WS Choir)”
is now recruiting new members for academic year 2026-27, and we warmly invite you to audition and become part of our vibrant musical community!
Founded in February 2012, the WS Choir will soon celebrate its 15th anniversary. With around 40 to 50 members each year, it is one of the University’s longest-established and largest student choirs. The Choir rehearses weekly at the College’s Music Centre and performs at College High Table Dinners, orientation activities, ceremonies and other special occasions. Each year culminates in our Annual Concert during the second term, where members showcase their musical development and share an exciting programme of performances with the University community.
Whether you are an experienced vocalist or someone who loves to sing, the choir offers a wonderful opportunity to develop your musical skills, perform at college and university events, and build friendships with fellow music enthusiasts across Woo Sing College and CUHK.
Audition Details:
25 August (Tue), 1:00 - 2:30 PM
8 September (Tue), 1:00 - 2:30 PM
10 September (Thu), 6:30 - 8:00 PM
Venue: Music Centre, Room G04, G/F, Lee Woo Sing College
To sign up for an audition slot, please complete the registration form (sign-in required):
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737334
You may find more information about WS Choir on our official website:
https://www.ws.cuhk.edu.hk/ws-choir/
Should you have any questions, feel free to contact us at:
wscollege@cuhk.edu.hk
.
We look forward to meeting you as a member of WS Choir!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Got a long document you need to review? Upload Word documents, PDFs, or text files directly into Copilot Chat and it will
read, summarize, analyze, or improve
them for you. Perfect for when you need to quickly get up to speed or polish a draft!
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"I've uploaded a 15-page project proposal. Please: (1) Give me a 3-sentence executive summary, (2) List the 5 most important points, (3) Identify any gaps or missing information that a reviewer might ask about, (4) Rate the overall persuasiveness on a scale of 1-10 and explain why, (5) Suggest 3 specific improvements to make it stronger."
Why this works:
Asking Copilot to critique AND suggest improvements turns it from a passive reader into an active editor. The rating scale adds a concrete benchmark so you know exactly where you stand!

Bonus tip:
For Legal
: "Upload a contract and ask 'What are the key obligations and risks?'"
For Marketing
: "Upload a campaign brief and ask 'Is the target audience clearly defined?'"
Want to enhance your Copilot skills? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

bodyText:

Midday Oasis: Healing Piano Concert   「午間心靈綠洲」:療癒鋼琴音樂會 - Chaplain's Office, Chung Chi College
From: Chaplain's Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chaplaincy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「午間心靈綠洲」
為大家預備一場為心靈而寫的原創鋼琴音樂會。
鋼琴家兼作曲家李丹以樹木、日落、雨水與雲彩為靈感，獻上全屬己出的鋼琴作品。慢慢展開自然的光影與氣息：枝葉的靜、暮色的暖、雨水的洗禮、雲層的流動。每一首作品都像一封寫給內心的短箋，讓聽者在午間稍停，把外面的節奏輕輕放下。
註冊音樂治療師張映瀅在樂曲之間以言語輕柔引導專注聆聽、呼吸與哼鳴托住旋律、與之同行，使言語與音樂合而為一。
聽、息、聲，三者在同一空間裡相遇。音樂打開心靈，靜默將它接住。聲響與靜默交織之處，身心得以稍歇、重整，找回平衡。
誠邀各位於星期一下午一時三十分，蒞臨香港中文大學崇基學院禮拜堂，與我們一同進入這段為心靈而設的音樂時光。
An original piano concert written for the inner life.
Pianist-composer Dan Lee presents works entirely her own, inspired by trees, sunsets, rain and clouds, unfolds instead as light and breath: the stillness of leaves, the warmth of dusk, the cleansing of rain, the drift of clouds. Each piece is a brief letter to the heart, inviting the listener to pause at midday and set down the outer pace.
Between the pieces, registered music therapist Rebecca Cheung offers spoken guidance in mindful listening, breathing and humming, hold it and walk with music, until speech and sound become one.
Listening, breath and tone meet in the same room. Music opens the spirit; stillness receives it. Where sound and silence are woven together, body and heart rest, realign and return to balance.
You are warmly invited this Monday at 1:30 p.m. to the Chung Chi College Chapel, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, to share this time of music written for the inner life.

Applications for the Language Exchange Programme (LEP) are now open!
Learning a language and culture is always better with friends.
The LEP is back and connects you with peers from diverse backgrounds for real conversations, meaningful cultural exchange and engaging activities along the way!
What to expect:
Practise your target language (English, Cantonese, Putonghua or more) in a natural relaxed setting
Build lasting friendships with students from all around the world
Share and explore cultural insights you won't find in a textbook
Join interactive activities designed to make language learning more enjoyable
Spots are limited — sign up now and start your LEP journey!

Join Social English Meet-up Club (SEMC): Meet Friends & Practise English for FREE!
Dear Students,
Want a cosy, pressure-free space to practise English, meet new friends, and join exciting workshops?
The Social English Meet-up Club (SEMC), run by the English Language Teaching Unit (ELTU) at CUHK, is officially recruiting for the 2026–2027 academic year—and you're invited!
Why Join the SEMC?
Priority Access: Be the first to grab spots for our highly popular workshops.
New ‘Read and Meet’ Initiative: Chat about interesting books, articles, and media in a completely relaxed, social setting. No exams, just great conversations!
Student Leader Initiative: Want to boost your CV? Help us plan and organise events to develop your leadership skills and earn an official ELTU Director’s Certificate.
Attendance Reward: Attend at least 80% of our gatherings this year and receive a certificate of recognition.
Best of all? Everything is completely free of charge! We welcome all CUHK students—whether local, international, undergraduate, or postgraduate.
Ready to Join Us?
It only takes a minute to sign up! Simply fill in
this online form
or scan the QR code below to become a member.
Let’s build a thriving, friendly English-speaking community together in CUHK!
Best regards,
The SEMC Team

title: Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :) English learning from computer-mediated English reading
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :) English learning from computer-mediated English reading  - Department of English
From: Jookyoung Jung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jookyoungjung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :)
English learning from computer-mediated English reading
Hello! I am Jookyoung Jung, Associate Professor at the Department of English. I'd like to invite you to a study that examines the relationship between computer-mediated English reading and English learning.
If you decide to participate, I will ask you to take part in three experimental sessions.
In Session 1, we will ask you to complete a brief questionnaire about yourself. Next, you will take English proficiency tests that measure your grammar and vocabulary.
In Session 2, you will read English texts while your eye movements are recorded using an eye-tracker.
In Session 3, you will take a series of memory tasks.
In return for your participation, I am able to offer you 300 HKD at the end of the 3rd session.
If you meet the criteria below, please join our study!
Your age is 18 years or older.
Chinese is your first language, and English is your second language.
Your English score (no lower, no higher!!): DSE English: 4-5; IELTS: 5.5-6.5; TOEFL iBT: 75-95; Cambridge English Scale: 160-180
If you want to participate in this study, please complete this online survey so that we can contact you and schedule your sessions.
Link:
https://forms.gle/9NyVzTHPBvW7wgHz6
If you have any queries about the study, please feel free to contact our team at tobiiproject2021@gmail.com. I would be very grateful if you would agree to take part! :-)
Jookyoung Jung
Associate Professor, Department of English
Chinese University of Hong Kong

園遊會分成四大區域，包括—
入宿寶物市集：
衣架？二手衫？刀叉杯碗碟？收納用品？這裡應有盡有！市集上的物品主要來自五月份退宿回收所得，有待你慧眼「尋寶」，免費取用。
減碳挑戰站：
現場特設「碳足跡小挑戰」，挑戰者一邊手捧與生活碳排放量等重的箱子，一邊參與Kahoot! 問答，爭取登上龍虎榜！
一擊即中回收球：
生活中哪些物資可以回收？在這個遊戲，參與者以投球判斷各類回收品，兩者都看得準並不容易。
流水式工作坊X2
：
場內更有專人教授綠色手作—天然防蚊液適用於中大多山多水的環境；而扭蛋殼多肉盆栽「的骰」易養，放在宿舍或辦公室皆適合！
記得9月10日11:00，龔約翰LG4見！
【Go Green Carnival】
Just moved into the student hostel and need some household items, but do not want to buy something brand new — then what next?
To raise students’ awareness of recycling materials and reducing carbon emissions, and to find new owners for items collected during the mid-year Hostel Checkout Recycling, the College Environment and Sustainable Development Committee will co-organise with Green@ShaTin the “Go Green Carnival” to make good use of resources and extend the spirit of environmental protection:
Date: 10 September (Thursday)            |         Time: 11:00-17:00
Venue: KSC LG4 Activity Room, Chung Chi College
The Carnival is composed of four sections, including—
Free Reuse Market:
Hangers? Clothes? Cutlery, cups, and dinnerware? Storage items? There are always things for everyone! Most of them come from the Hostel Checkout Recycling collections in May.
Low-Carbon Challenge:
Challengers are invited to bear weight equivalent to carbon emissions in living, and at the same time take part in Kahoot! quizzes to compete in the leaderboard!
Eco Ball Tossing:
Participants will judge different recyclable items by throwing balls — getting both right is not as easy as it sounds.
Ongoing workshop x2:
Participants will be instructed in two DIY workshops — making natural bug spray suited to the CUHK environment and planting succulents in capsules that are easy to care for in hostels and offices.
Remember 11 am on 10 September. See you at KSC LG4!

Announcements
Recruiting Young Adults (18-29 years old) in Hong Kong for Participating a Bereavement Survey Study (receive up to HKD300 supermarket coupon upon completion!!) 誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券) - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Ling Haofeng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券)
參加者納入標準：
18
至
29
歲
在香港居住的本地年輕成人
在過去
18
個月內經歷過親友
/
重要的人離世
能閱懂中文和以廣東話溝通
研究程序：
1
）基線問卷
填妥同意書後，參加者將完成一份20分鐘基線問卷
問卷問題將與面對及經歷親友/重要的人離世時的哀傷過程及對死亡的觀念有關
完成基線問卷將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
2
）第一輪跟進問卷
六個月後，我們會邀請參加者完成一份跟進問卷
完成第一輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
3
）第二輪跟進問卷
在完成第一輪跟進問卷的六個月後，我們會邀請參加者再次完成一份跟進問卷
完成第二輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
本研究均屬自願參與。研究資料會被保密，除研究人員外，任何人均不能獲取參與者所填寫的問卷資訊或錄音內容。本研究已通過香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會(CREC-2025.748)及香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理(SBRE‐24‐0378)審查。
參加方法:
請用以下連結填寫同意書及問卷，完成後可獲送贈港幣
一百元
正超市禮券
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊合資格的香港年輕成人。
如有查詢，請與博士後研究員凌皓峰博士聯絡。
電郵: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp: 44643831

歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊合資格的香港年輕成人。
如有查詢，請與博士後研究員凌皓峰博士聯絡。
電郵: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.

NEWLY LAUNCHED! - UGEB2996 Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist (Fully Online & Asynchronous Learning) 全新推出！UGEB2996 初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色 (全網上非同步學習) - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。
課程特色
自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

UGEB2996

Course Title:
Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

Mode:
Online Asynchronous

Credits:
1 Unit

Sustainable Development Goals × General Education (SDG Study Scheme) – Start Your Sustainability Journey in the new academic year!   - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education

SDG Study Scheme
– Learn. Act. Achieve
Are you passionate about sustainability and making a real impact?
Join the
SDG Study Scheme
by the Office of University General Education (OUGE) – a unique opportunity to integrate the
United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
into your General Education journey at CUHK!

Why Join?
The SDG Study Scheme empowers you with essential knowledge and practical experience for tackling the challenges of tomorrow. This is your chance to showcase your sustainability competency and potential! Let’s be part of a community striving for a better future together!

What’s in the Scheme?
The SDG Study Scheme comprises three components, combining knowledge-based learning with experiential learning:
1.
Understand SDGs with a global vision
Finish the short online introductory course -
How to Achieve the SDGs
by the SDG Academy, and
pass
a
short
quiz
on the
SDG Community Blackboard site
.
2.
Equip yourself with SDG-related k
nowledge
Take
two to three
SDG-GE
(General Education) courses
, each carrying at least 2 units
:
Students admitted in
2021-22
: take at least
3
SDG-GE courses
Students admitted in
2022-23 or after
: take at least
2
SDG-GE courses
3.
Take action to help the communities
Complete one of the following action items:
one
SDG-SE (Social Engagement) course
of at least 2 units
; or
at least 26 hours
of co-curricular
Volunteer Activity (SDG-VA)
.
Learn more:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/sdg-study-scheme-overview/

Certification
Upon completing the Scheme, you will be awarded the
SDG Explorer Certificate
to recognize your achievements in both SDG knowledge and community engagement.
Apply for your certificate here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=12998341

Actions to take!
1. Join the SDG Community!
Join the SDG Community to connect with like-minded students and receive updates on SDG-related activities and the SDG Study Scheme.
Sign up here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=10231196
2. Enroll in SDG courses in Term 1!
Take your GE studies further – enroll in courses labelled with SDGs.
These courses not only enrich your sustainability competency but also empower you to engage with global and local sustainability challenges through meaningful learning and actions.
Browse the list of SDG-related GE courses offered in Term 1 and enroll early:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/wp-content/uploads/learning/2627T1_SDG-Class-Offerings.pdf
3. Follow us on Instagram and share with your friends!
Connect with us on Instagram at @
sdg_ge_cuhk
and scan the QR code below to follow us.

Enquiry
Email us at:
sdg-ouge@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
Undergraduate students wanted for a FYP survey analysing whether CUHK canteens can handle the demands in the future  - Chung Chi College
From: Chiu Kwok Shing, with endorsement of the course supervisor Dr. Ng Chi Kong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155212981@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Hello, we are students from GECC4130. We noticed that there are quite some
changes for student canteens in CUHK over the years, and wondered whether
the current situation could meet the future demand. As Chung Chi College,
Wu Yee Sun College, and Shaw College are building additional hostels
currently, and there will be one more postgraduate student hostel, we are
afraid that more students living on campus will overwhelm the student
canteens. Therefore, we would like to collect data about the general
experience of undergraduate students at university outlets as well as how
additional hostels may affect the demand for CUHK canteen services.
If you find our study meaningful or would like to share your
experience/opinion with us to let more people know how the catering
services in CUHK are doing, we would be grateful that you could spend some
time taking the following survey:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cAuL2gHWQdbgGyO
If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to contact
1155212981@link.cuhk.edu.hk (Ken). Thank you!

二
○
二六至二七年度「新亞書院文化講座」第一講
「新亞書院文化講座」由香港中文大學新亞書院與新亞書院校友會合辦、新亞中學協辦，每年舉辦兩至三次講座。本年度第一場講座將於二Ｏ二六年九月十九日舉行，主講嘉賓為張倩儀博士。講座詳情如下：
講題：絲路上不容錯過的訊息
講者：張倩儀博士 (中大校友，文化學者、出版人及遊記作家)
主持：陳柏嘉博士 (香港中文大學新亞書院文化講座委員會成員、香港中文大學自學中心講師)

Join the CUHK International Connection Programme as a Mentee   - Office of Student Affairs
From: Learning and Cultural Enhancement Section
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
lces@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The International Connection Programme (ICP) is a cross-cultural peer mentorship programme organized by the Office of Student Affairs, which offers a unique opportunity for students from diverse backgrounds to connect and enhance cultural understanding. We warmly invite you to join us as a mentee, where you will have the chance to:
Build intercultural mentoring networks by connecting with senior students
Facilitate your transition and adjustment to the university life
Engage in enriching cross-cultural interactions and contribute to a more culturally inclusive and diverse campus
Eligibility
Year 1 non-local undergraduate students who will be studying at CUHK in both terms of 2026-27.
Matching
In each group, two mentors will be matched up with approximately four mentees.
Content
1.
Training Day Camp
All participants will be required to attend the training day camp. Free of charge.
Date: 4 October 2026 (Sunday)
Time: 9:00am – 4:00pm (Round-trip transportation will be arranged)
Location: Tai Po
Content: Ice-breaking, team building, cross-cultural communication skills, global leadership development
2. Bonding and cultural activities initiated by your group
3. Engaging cultural events organized by the Office of Student Affairs
4. Visit to CUHK (Shenzhen)
5. Leadership and Cultural tour
Certification and Prize
Student Development Portfolio (SDP) record update
Certificate of Appreciation (Requirement: attendance in the training day camp, one LCES-endorsed activity, completion of self-initiated cultural activity and submission of report)
(For selected teams)
Leadership and cultural tour in 2027
Apply now to be part of this enriching initiative!

Master of Arts in Japanese Studies (2027-2028 intake) is now open for application!
We are pleased to announce that applications are now open for the 2027–28 Master of Arts in Japanese Studies (MAJS) Programme.
Our MAJS Programme offers comprehensive training in Japanese society, culture, history, and language. Designed for those seeking deeper academic engagement or professional opportunities related to Japan, the programme equips students with the knowledge and skills essential for careers in Japan-related fields or further academic pursuits.
Whether you're passionate about Japanese studies or planning a career with a Japan focus, this programme is your gateway to meaningful growth and development.
For more information about the programme, please visit:
https://www.jas.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/programmes/ma-in-japanese-studies/

1st round: 30 September 2026

Announcements
{New Term, New Reads} Up to 25% Off at CUHK Press {開Sem大放送} 中大山上有個小書店 - CUP
From: Leung King Hung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

(See English ver. below)
開Sem大放送：中大山上有個小書店
中大迎新與開學的季節又到來，位於山腰的中大出版社小書店很想跟大家打招呼！
為了鼓勵大家坐 3 分鐘校巴，或爬 5 分鐘山路走到「何東夫人堂」，看看出版社的書與一系列文創產品，我們在 9 月 7 日至 9 月 25 日期間，特別準備了「中大人限定」的開Sem見面禮三重奏：
1⃣
精神福袋（免費拎）
•
來了就送
：$30 現金券 + 小書店探訪指南 + 隨機好禮（如 Reading Trail 運動毛巾）
•
打卡再送
：於 IG / Threads / 小紅書 / 朋友圈打卡，再送香港作家西西「朋友的貓」系列襟章（蹲貓、懶貓、企貓、睡貓）
2⃣
一籃子 75 折選書
• 特別優惠
：中大人平日享 8 折，活動期間 12 本精選好書加碼至
75 折
！（把握 add-drop period 的歡樂時光⋯⋯）
•
精選書單
：《我這一代人》、《尋找國家中的婦女》、《灣區變形》、《新家庭主義興衰》、《Hong Kong Art Deco Architecture》、《供水香港》、《大學的讀法》、《種植生活》、《從彼島到此島》、《清音與破曉》、《歷史學的訓練》、《虛擬親密》
3⃣
小書店印章放題
• 歷年「她的現代史」、「小王子的領悟」、「香港原生植物」、「小書店/何東夫人堂」、「閱讀不用等待」、「香港街市」等全套紀念印章一次過登場，歡迎帶手帳來蓋好蓋滿！

地點
：何東夫人堂地下小書店 （
Google Maps
）

日期
：9 月 7 日 至 9 月 25 日
⏰
時間
：星期一至五 10:30–12:30 | 14:30–17:30（星期六至日一般休息）
歡迎大家來，也歡迎關注我們的
Instagram（@cuhkpress）
！
———————————————

New Term, New Reads: Up to 25% Off at CUHK Press
As the new term kick off, the CUHK Press's bookstore "CUP Corner" at Lady Ho Tung Hall is excited to welcome you back! Take a 3-minute shuttle or a 5-minute walk up the hill to enjoy our
Back-to-School Trio Offer
from September 7 to September 25:
1⃣
Free Goodie Bag
•
Come & Get
: Free $30 cash voucher, bookstore guide, and a mystery gift (e.g., Reading Trail sports towel)
•
Cat Pins!
: Post on IG, Threads, RedNote, or WeChat to claim a limited-edition Xi Xi "Friend's Cat" enamel pin (crouching, lazy, standing, or sleeping cat)
2⃣
25% Off 12 Selected Titles
• Upgrade your regular 20% CUHK discount to
25% off
on 12 curated titles—perfect for add-drop period
3⃣
Stamp Station
• Bring your journal, enjoy unlimited access to all available commemorative stamps

Location:
CUP Corner, CUHK Press, Lady Ho Tung Hall, CUHK (
Google Maps
)

Dates:
Sept 7 – Sept 25
⏰
Hours:
Mon–Fri 10:30–12:30 | 14:30–17:30 (Normally closed on Sat & Sun)
Follow our
Instagram (@cuhkpress)
!

HIST2501GL    Hong Kong History in the Field
This course will introduce the history of Hong Kong by focusing on its “fields.” It will examine how various field sites such as temples, museums, historical trails, renovated historical buildings, and even internets could be used to understand the history of different places, events, and people in Hong Kong from the ancient period to the present.

The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260907)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 7 September to 11 September: (1) Discussion Skills and Current Affairs - Speaking with Confidence, (2) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills, (3) Study Skills in English at University Level, and (4) Saying What You Mean - English Pronunciation for Cantonese and Mandarin Speakers. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
7 September (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
9 September (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
11 September (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 7 September to 11 September: (1) CRE Vocabulary and the Use of Idioms, (2) JRE Argumentative Writing II, and (3) BLNST Basic Law Test. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心九月七日至九月十一日舉辦 (1) 公務員綜合招聘試系列(CRE)：現代漢語詞匯與成語的運用, (2) 公務員綜合招聘考試系列(CRE)：能力傾向測試, (3) CRE中文運用應試實戰班：閱讀理解 (粵), (4) JRE 議論文寫作(II), 及 (5) BLNST基本法及香港國安法測試 (國安法部份)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於九月七日至九月十一日提供以下中文輔導時段。
7 September (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
8 September (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
9 September (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
10 September (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted

Regarding Student-led Activities on campus
As the new semester begins, student groups are planning to organize and host various activities on campus. The University reminds all students that any activities conducted on campus must be approved in advance by the relevant departments. All students must adhere to the proper procedures when organizing events to ensure compliance with university regulations. The University reserves the right to prohibit any unauthorized activities on campus. Students are also advised not to participate in any events that have not been approved by the University.
Wishing you a smooth and fulfilling campus life in the new academic year!
Office of Student Affairs

For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您好！心理學系與香港理工大學應用社會科學系研究團隊正合作進行一項香港大學生的文化多樣性與適應研究 ，誠邀您參與。
研究目的是探討香港高等院校學生的文化背景對學業、社會適應等方面的影響，為政策及支援提出發展建議。本研究已獲得香港理工大學倫理委員會的批准（參考編號：HSEARS20250122009）。
參與條件如下：
18歲或以上
現就讀於教資會資助大學（即香港八大其中之一）
本科的全日制學生*，本地與非本地生皆可
能以中文或英文進行閱讀、書寫與交流
*兼讀制學生、交換生和副學位課程的學生不符合參與條
件
研究活動：
網上問卷調查（2026年9月10日截止報名）
問卷包含有關文化取向與認同、語言能力、心理與社會適應、政策態度、健康狀況等方面的問題，完成需時約45分鐘，可於方便的時間自行填寫。完成後可獲得津貼HKD100，將以轉數快或Payme派發。
若有興趣參與，請填寫報名表：
https://hkpuhealthandsocial.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ctN4pvNb9g8jGyq
如有查詢，請聯絡心理學系湯俊逸教授(
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或 理工大學研究人員陸依晴博士(電郵：
erin.lu@polyu.edu.hk
)。
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hello! Department of Psychology is collaborating with the Department of Applied Social Sciences at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) on a study on Cultural Diversity and Adaptation among University Students in Hong Kong. We sincerely invites you to participate in this study.
The study aims to examine how university students’ cultural backgrounds influence their academic and social adaptation at Hong Kong’s universities and to generate insights to inform the development of relevant policies and support measures. This study has been approved by the Human Subjects Ethics Application Review System (HSEARS) of PolyU (Reference No.: HSEARS20250122009).
Eligibility criteria:
Aged 18 or above
Currently studying at a UGC‑funded university (i.e., one of Hong Kong’s eight public universities)
Full‑time undergraduate student*, either local or non-local
Able to read, write, and communicate in Chinese or English
*Part‑time students, exchange students, and students of sub-degree programs are not eligible.
Research activity:
Online Survey (Registration Closes on 10 September 2026)
The survey includes questions about cultural orientation and identity, language proficiency, psychological and social adaptation, policy attitudes, health conditions, etc. It takes about 45 minutes to complete, and participants can complete in their own time. Upon completion, you will receive an HKD 100 allowance, which will be distributed via FPS or PayMe.
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the registration form:
https://hkpuhealthandsocial.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ctN4pvNb9g8jGyq
For inquiries, please contact Prof. Alan Tong at Department of Psychology (
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
) or Dr Erin Lu (
erin.lu@polyu.edu.hk
) at PolyU.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Calling All Student Helpers — Join Us at the ILC Booth Next Week!  🎉🍦學生助理招募中 — 下星期來自學中心攤位玩啦！ 🎪 - Independent Learning Centre (ILC)
From: Independent Learning Centre (ILC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

學生助理招募中
—
下星期來自學中心攤位玩啦！

主辦單位：自學中心 (ILC, CUHK)
新學年想找一份輕鬆有趣的校園工作嗎？快來加入 ILC舉辦的推廣攤位活動！這是一個提升溝通技巧、認識新朋友、感受校園活力的好機會。如果你能以廣東話、普通話及英語交流，又享受與人互動，這份工作絕對適合你！而且，薪酬更高於標準學生助理時薪。我們現正限量招募，快邀請朋友一同報名，名額有限。

工作詳情
日期：2026年9月8日及10日（星期二及四）
⏰ 時間：上午11時至下午2時（每天3小時，共6小時）
地點：康本國際學術園廣場（YIA Piazza）

工作內容
向同學派發單張及雪糕杯
介紹及推廣 ILC 的精彩活動及課程
主持趣味小測驗，與同學互動交流
協助推廣 ILC 社交媒體，吸引更多追蹤者

我們希望你
友善、外向、善於與人相處
能流利運用廣東話、普通話及英語
不介意於戶外工作
歡迎本科生及研究生申請

心動了嗎？
立即電郵報名至：
eli.poon@cuhk.edu.hk
Enquiry: 3943 8720

Calling All Student Helpers — Join Us at the ILC Booth Next Week!

Organizer: Independent Learning Centre (ILC)
Looking for a fun, flexible, and rewarding way to spend a few hours on campus? Come join the ILC promotional booth at the YIA Piazza next week (8 & 10 Sept, Tue & Thu) — a great opportunity to sharpen your communication skills, connect with fellow students, and be part of the campus buzz!
If you enjoy meeting new people and are comfortable chatting in Cantonese, Putonghua, and English, this one is for you. Best of all, you'll earn
above the standard student helper rate
! We're batch hiring, so grab your friends and apply early before spots fill up!

Job Details
Dates: 8 & 10 September 2026 (Tue & Thur)
⏰ Time: 11 AM – 2 PM (3 hours per day, 6 hrs total)
Location: YIA Piazza

What You'll Do
Hand out leaflets and ice-cream cups to students
Share and introduce exciting ILC activities and events
Host fun short quizzes to connect with students
Help grow our social media community

What We're Looking For
Friendly, outgoing, and approachable
Fluent in Cantonese, Putonghua, and English
Comfortable working outdoors
Open to both undergraduate and postgraduate students

Ready to Join?
Email your application to:
eli.poon@cuhk.edu.hk
Enquiry: 3943 8720
